reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:11:1. [blocking] — Claude Code adapter — “`Stop` | Primary mechanical checkpoint” misses limit failures: API errors fire `StopFailure` instead, with structured error fields; `Stop` does not run. Thus Tier A cannot detect its defining failure path. Add `StopFailure`, classify its `error`/`error_details`/`last_assistant_message`, checkpoint fail-open, and test every documented error type. [Claude hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#stopfailure).
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:13:2. [blocking] — Codex adapter — “no lifecycle hooks exist” and reliance on “`~/.codex/prompts` slash commands” are obsolete assumptions. Current Codex exposes stable lifecycle hooks and plugins, while custom prompts are deprecated. Redesign around a Codex plugin/project hooks and skills; cut the notify shim and prompts from the primary path, retaining prompts only as a documented legacy fallback. [Codex hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks), [custom-prompts deprecation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/custom-prompts).
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:15:3. [blocking] — Core bundle — “single active bundle” plus “append-only events” has no locking or compare-and-swap protocol. Two sessions can interleave journal writes, overwrite snapshots, reuse sequence numbers, or receive the same bundle. Add a repo-scoped lock/lease, writer/session IDs, monotonic sequence allocation, stale-lock recovery, and concurrency/process-kill tests. Multi-bundle UI can remain v2.
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:17:4. [major] — Build order — “full module APIs, per-module test lists…specified in the core design” references material absent from this plan, preventing dependency review. The sequence also builds `checkpoint cmd` before `git snapshot`, although checkpoints require git state, and claims dogfooded templates “from day one” while implementing templates near the end. Incorporate the missing design, move git snapshot before checkpoint, and establish templates/scaffold once rather than twice.
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:19:5. [major] — Core/Receive — “persists a `roles.remap` journal event” occurs before successful acknowledgement, while only Claude’s adapter “flips bundle to `received`.” Cancellation, unavailable roles, or concurrent receivers leave partial state. Make receive a core-owned prepare/commit transaction with a receipt token, atomic state transition, retry semantics, and identical behavior across adapters.
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:21:6. [major] — Sandbox and repository assumptions — “mechanical git state is always re-derived” assumes a writable git worktree. Read-only harness sandboxes cannot write `.handoff/`; non-git directories, nested monorepo launches, linked worktrees, and multiple roots are undefined. Specify root discovery and precedence, graceful non-git mode, permission-denied behavior, and a user-executed fallback when agent writes are unavailable.
reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-01/verdict.md:23:7. [major] — Bundle/recovery — “append-only journal” has no rotation or size bound, yet full recovery replays it forever. Frequent hooks make startup and rebuild increasingly expensive, and concurrent compaction is unspecified. docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:48:_(Sections below synthesized from two Plan-agent designs — core engine; adapters/templates/methodology — merged after Gate-1 review.)_
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:54:**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:56:**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:60:**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:62:**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:64:**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:66:**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:68:**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:70:**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:72:**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:74:**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:76:**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:78:Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:81:- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:82:- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.

reviews/2026-07-11-baton-v1-plan/gate-1-plan/iteration-03/verdict.md:12:1. [blocking] — Core engine / Concurrency — “re-verifies the holder’s token immediately before acting” does not close the check-then-write race: a writer can verify, pause, be replaced after 60 seconds, then resume and mutate state after the new owner acquires the lock. Fencing tokens alone cannot make filesystem writes conditional. — Do not steal merely by heartbeat age. Record host plus process-instance identity and auto-recover only when the owner is provably dead; otherwise require explicit forced recovery. Add a test pausing the owner after its final token check, not merely before it.

    31	// without mistaking a flag's value for a positional. Keep in sync with the

    33	const STRING_FLAGS = new Set(['root', 'approve-smoke']);
    34	
    35	/**
    36	 * `baton loop <subcommand>` — the Layer-2 goal-loop surface. v1 subcommands:
    37	 * `init "<goal>"` (scaffold loop.json; two-phase, idempotent, dry-run-able).
    38	 * Supervisor-side by design: the BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD guard deliberately
    39	 * does NOT apply here.
    40	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    41	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    42	 */
    43	export async function cmdLoop(args, io) {
    44	  /** @type {string[]} */
    45	  const positionals = [];
    46	  /** @type {string[]} */
    47	  const flagTokens = [];
    48	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    49	    const a = args[i];
    50	    if (typeof a === 'string' && a.startsWith('--')) {
    51	      flagTokens.push(a);
    52	      if (STRING_FLAGS.has(a.slice(2)) && i + 1 < args.length) {
    53	        i += 1;
    54	        flagTokens.push(args[i]);
    55	      }
    56	    } else {
    57	      positionals.push(a);
    58	    }
    59	  }
    60	
    61	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(flagTokens, { 'dry-run': 'boolean', 'approve-smoke': 'string' });
    62	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'loop', parsed.error);
    63	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    64	
    65	  const sub = positionals[0];
    66	  if (sub === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'a subcommand is required — try: baton loop init "<goal>" or baton loop run');
    67	  if (sub === 'run' || sub === 'resume') {
    68	    if (positionals.length > 1) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unexpected argument '${positionals[1]}'`);
    69	    if (flags['approve-smoke'] === '') return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', '--approve-smoke requires a value (the token from smoke-approval.json)');
    70	    if (sub === 'resume') flags.__resume = true;
    71	    return runLoop(flags, io);
    72	  }
    73	  if (sub !== 'init') return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unknown subcommand '${sub}' (supported: init, run, resume)`);
    74	
    75	  const goal = positionals[1];
    76	  if (goal === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'loop init requires a goal — baton loop init "<goal>"');
    77	  if (positionals.length > 2) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unexpected argument '${positionals[2]}'`);
    78	
    79	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    80	  const path = `${root}/loop.json`;
    81	
    82	  const finish = (/** @type {any} */ data, /** @type {string} */ human) => {
    83	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data });
    84	    else io.stdout.write(`${human}\n`);
    85	    return 0;
    86	  };
    87	
    88	  // Idempotent: an existing spec is the user's — never overwritten.
    89	  if (io.fs.existsSync(path)) {
    90	    return finish({ created: false, path }, `baton loop init: ${path} already exists — left untouched`);
    91	  }
    92	  if (flags['dry-run'] === true) {
    93	    return finish(
    94	      { created: false, path, dryRun: true },
    95	      `baton loop init (dry-run): would write ${path} — the default baton/loop@1 spec with goal "${goal}"`,
    96	    );
    97	  }
    98	  ensureDir(io.fs, root);
    99	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, path, defaultLoopSpec(goal));
   100	  return finish({ created: true, path }, `baton loop init: wrote ${path} (goal "${goal}") — edit constraints/smoke, then run baton loop run`);
   101	}

   103	// Exit codes for `loop run` (frozen by the loop-run test contract):
   104	// 0 done / awaiting-smoke-approval · 1 live-lock refusal · 2 usage error ·
   105	// 3 escalated · 4 parked.
   106	const EXIT_ESCALATED = 3;
   107	const EXIT_PARKED = 4;
   108	
   109	/** @param {any} g */
   110	const gitHeadOf = (g) => g?.headSha ?? 'none';
   111	/** @param {any} g */
   112	const gitContentOf = (g) => g?.contentDigest ?? dedupeKey(g ?? null);
   113	
   114	/**
   115	 * Acquire the supervisor run lock ATOMICALLY (exclusive create — never
   116	 * check-then-write, which loses a race by clobbering the winner). A live
   117	 * owner refuses; a provably-dead one is reclaimed: its recorded in-flight
   118	 * child groups (.handoff/loop/children.ndjson) are KILLED first so no
   119	 * orphan survives the takeover, then the lock is retried once.
   120	 * Shared by `loop run` and `pipeline run`.
   121	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {string} cmdLabel
   122	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true, release: () => void} | {ok: false, code: number}>}
   123	 */
   124	export async function acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, cmdLabel) {
   125	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   126	  const lockPath = `${p.dir}/supervisor.lock`;
   127	  const childrenPath = `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`;
   128	  ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   129	  const payload = JSON.stringify({ host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime, runId: `sup-${io.pid}` });
   130	
   131	  const tryExclusive = () => {
   132	    // Fast-path an already-present lock (fakes without O_EXCL semantics rely
   133	    // on this); the wx flag below is the REAL exclusivity on a POSIX fs — a
   134	    // competitor that lands between the check and the write throws EEXIST
   135	    // instead of being clobbered.
   136	    if (io.fs.existsSync(lockPath)) return false;
   137	    try {
   138	      io.fs.writeFileSync(lockPath, payload, { flag: 'wx' });
   139	      return true;
   140	    } catch (err) {
   141	      if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') return false;
   142	      throw err;
   143	    }
   144	  };
   145	
   146	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt += 1) {
   147	    if (tryExclusive()) {
   148	      // A fresh acquisition owns a fresh child registry: prior invocations'
   149	      // start/retire records are truncated so a stale retire can never mask a
   150	      // later in-flight child that reuses the same childId (I2).
   151	      try {
   152	        if (io.fs.existsSync(childrenPath)) io.fs.unlinkSync(childrenPath);
   153	      } catch {
   154	        // Best effort.
   155	      }
   156	      return {
   157	        ok: true,
   158	        release: () => {
   159	          try {
   160	            if (io.fs.existsSync(lockPath)) io.fs.unlinkSync(lockPath);
   161	          } catch {
   162	            // Best effort — a stale lock is recoverable via the dead path.
   163	          }
   164	        },
   165	      };
   166	    }
   167	    const existing = safeReadJson(io.fs, lockPath);
   168	    const other = existing.ok ? existing.value : null;
   169	    // Liveness verifies the (pid, startTime) PAIR — a recycled pid without the
   170	    // recorded start time is a dead owner, not a live supervisor (I5).
   171	    const alive = other && typeof other.pid === 'number' && typeof io.processAlive === 'function' ? io.processAlive(other.pid, other.startTime) : true;
   172	    const sameProcess = other && other.pid === io.pid && other.startTime === io.startTime;
   173	    if (!sameProcess && (!other || other.host !== io.host || alive)) {
   174	      io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: another supervisor (pid ${other?.pid ?? 'unknown'} on ${other?.host ?? 'unknown'}, run ${other?.runId ?? '?'}) holds the run lock — refusing a second supervisor\n`);
   175	      return { ok: false, code: 1 };
   176	    }
   177	    // Provably dead (or our own stale lock): reap its recorded in-flight
   178	    // child groups BEFORE anything else runs, then reclaim.
   179	    if (io.fs.existsSync(childrenPath)) {
   180	      const lines = String(io.fs.readFileSync(childrenPath, 'utf8')).split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim() !== '');
   181	      // Match retires to starts IN ORDER per childId — a resumed invocation
   182	      // reuses childIds, and a prior run's retire must never mask the newer
   183	      // in-flight start of the same id (I2). Whatever start remains unmatched
   184	      // is genuinely in-flight.
   185	      /** @type {Map<string, any[]>} */
   186	      const inflight = new Map();
   187	      for (const line of lines) {
   188	        try {
   189	          const rec = JSON.parse(line);
   190	          if (typeof rec?.endedAt === 'string') inflight.get(rec.childId)?.shift();
   191	          else if (typeof rec?.pgid === 'number') {
   192	            if (!inflight.has(rec.childId)) inflight.set(rec.childId, []);
   193	            inflight.get(rec.childId)?.push(rec);
   194	          }
   195	        } catch {
   196	          // A torn record is unreapable — skip it.
   197	        }
   198	      }
   199	      // Kill ONLY genuinely in-flight children (start with no matching
   200	      // retire): a retired child's pgid may have been recycled by an
   201	      // unrelated live process — killing it would be a pid-reuse casualty (H3).
   202	      for (const recs of inflight.values()) {
   203	        for (const rec of recs) {
   204	          if (typeof io.processAlive === 'function' && io.processAlive(rec.pgid)) {
   205	            if (typeof io.processKill === 'function') io.processKill(-rec.pgid, 'SIGKILL');
   206	          }
   207	        }
   208	      }
   209	      try {
   210	        io.fs.unlinkSync(childrenPath);
   211	      } catch {
   212	        // Best effort.
   213	      }
   214	    }
   215	    io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: reclaimed the run lock from a provably-dead supervisor (pid ${other?.pid})\n`);
   216	    try {
   217	      io.fs.unlinkSync(lockPath);
   218	    } catch {
   219	      // Already gone.
   220	    }
   221	  }
   222	  io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmdLabel}: could not acquire the run lock after reclaiming — another supervisor keeps winning\n`);
   223	  return { ok: false, code: 1 };
   224	}
   225	
   226	/**
   227	 * The supervisor state machine: drives the spec's phases through headless
   228	 * role children, records every transition in the journal-replayable loop
   229	 * state, enforces the 5-cap, pauses at the smoke gate, and hands limit
   230	 * deaths to the failover transaction. Children run via the injectable seam
   231	 * `io.superviseChild ?? superviseChild`.
   232	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags @param {any} io
   233	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   234	 */
   235	async function runLoop(flags, io) {
   236	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
   237	  const specPath = `${root}/loop.json`;
   238	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   239	  const lockPath = `${p.dir}/supervisor.lock`;
   240	
   241	  // Preconditions — before any lock or spawn.
   242	  const rawSpec = safeReadJson(io.fs, specPath);
   243	  if (!rawSpec.ok) {
   244	    return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `no loop.json at ${specPath} — scaffold one with: baton loop init "<goal>"`);
   245	  }
   246	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   247	  if (!config) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `no readable baton.config.json at ${root} — the role matrix is required`);
   248	  const validated = validateLoopSpec(rawSpec.value, config);
   249	  if (validated.ok !== true) {
   250	    return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `loop.json is invalid:\n  - ${validated.errors.join('\n  - ')}`);
   251	  }
   252	  const spec = validated.spec;
   253	
   254	  // Supervisor run lock — atomic exclusive acquisition; provably-dead owners
   255	  // are reclaimed with their recorded child groups reaped first (B8 + G4).
   256	  const lock = await acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, 'loop run');
   257	  if (lock.ok !== true) return lock.code;
   258	
   259	  // Load or initialize the run state — stamped with {flavor, specDigest} so
   260	  // cross-flavor, changed-spec, or pre-stamp resumes refuse instead of
   261	  // misaligning (H5 + I3). These refusals release the lock explicitly — an
   262	  // early return here must not leave supervisor.lock behind (I4).
   263	  const specDigest = dedupeKey(spec.phases);
   264	  let { state } = await loadLoopState(root, io);
   265	  if (state === null) {
   266	    // A resume with nothing persisted is a wrong-directory mistake, not a
   267	    // fresh run — refusing beats silently initializing and running (N2).
   268	    if (flags.__resume === true) {
   269	      lock.release();
   270	      return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'nothing to resume — no run state exists here; start with: baton loop run');
   271	    }
   272	    state = { ...initLoopState(spec, io), flavor: 'loop', specDigest };
   273	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   274	  } else {
   275	    if (typeof state.flavor === 'string' && state.flavor !== 'loop') {
   276	      lock.release();
   277	      return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `the persisted run state is flavor '${state.flavor}' — a ${state.flavor} run cannot be resumed as a loop (flavor mismatch); archive .handoff/loop or finish the ${state.flavor} run first`);
   278	    }
   279	    if (typeof state.flavor !== 'string' || typeof state.specDigest !== 'string') {
   280	      lock.release();
   281	      return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'the persisted run state is missing its {flavor, specDigest} stamp (pre-stamp legacy state) — resuming it could misalign the run; archive .handoff/loop to start fresh');
   282	    }
   283	    if (state.specDigest !== specDigest) {
   284	      lock.release();
   285	      return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'loop.json phases changed since this run started (spec digest mismatch) — resuming would misalign the phase position; archive .handoff/loop to start fresh');
   286	    }
   287	  }
   288	  const runId = state.runId;
   289	  // The lock payload's runId now correlates with the run it guards (H8).
   290	  io.fs.writeFileSync(`${p.dir}/supervisor.lock`, JSON.stringify({ host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime, runId }));
   291	
   292	  /** Apply one event, journal it, persist the snapshot — one transition. */
   293	  const transition = async (/** @type {any} */ ev) => {
   294	    const next = applyLoopEvent(state, ev);
   295	    const seq = await appendLoopEvent(root, ev, io);
   296	    state = { ...next, journalSeq: seq };
   297	    await writeLoopState(root, state, io);
   298	    return state;
   299	  };
   300	
   301	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
   302	  const runner = io.superviseChild ?? superviseChild;
   303	  // The runId is already 'loop-<hex>' — no extra prefix (D5).
   304	  const sessionHint = runId;
   305	  /** @type {string[]} */
   306	  let avoid = [];
   307	  /** @type {Array<{platform: string, model: string}>} */
   308	  let avoidEntries = [];
   309	  let childSeq = 0;
   310	
   311	  try {
   312	    // `loop resume` — a PARK is resumable; an escalation is operator-only.
   313	    if (flags.__resume === true) {
   314	      if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   315	        io.stderr.write(`baton loop resume: the run is ESCALATED (gate ${state.escalation?.gate}) — escalation is an operator decision; resolve the findings and start a fresh gate instead\n`);
   316	        return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   317	      }
   318	      if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) {
   319	        await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.RESUME });
   320	        io.stdout.write('baton loop resume: the parked run is running again\n');
   321	      }
   322	    }
   323	
   324	    // --approve-smoke: verify the presented token against RECOMPUTED inputs;
   325	    // drift parks (the human approved a state that no longer exists).
   326	    if (typeof flags['approve-smoke'] === 'string') {
   327	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) {
   328	        return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `--approve-smoke only applies while the run awaits smoke approval (status: ${state.status})`);
   329	      }
   330	      const record = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json`);
   331	      if (!record.ok) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'no smoke-approval.json found — run the loop to the smoke gate first');
   332	      const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   333	      const currentInputs = {
   334	        stateDigest: dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(p.state, 'utf8')),
   335	        smokeCmd: String(spec.smoke?.cmd ?? ''),
   336	        smokeOutputDigest: String(record.value?.inputs?.smokeOutputDigest ?? ''),
   337	        gitHead: gitHeadOf(git),
   338	        gitContentDigest: gitContentOf(git),
   339	        childAssignment: String(record.value?.inputs?.childAssignment ?? ''),
   340	      };
   341	      const verify = verifySmokeToken(String(flags['approve-smoke']), currentInputs);
   342	      if (verify.ok !== true) {
   343	        const drifted = 'driftedInputs' in verify ? verify.driftedInputs.join(', ') : 'unknown';
   344	        await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: `smoke approval token is stale — drifted inputs: ${drifted}; re-run the smoke gate` });
   345	        io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: smoke approval REFUSED — inputs drifted since the token was issued (${drifted}); the run is parked for a fresh smoke pass\n`);
   346	        return EXIT_PARKED;
   347	      }
   348	      await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_APPROVE, token: flags['approve-smoke'], verified: true });
   349	      io.stdout.write('baton loop run: smoke approval verified — continuing the run\n');
   350	    }
   351	
   352	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   353	      io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: the run is escalated (gate ${state.escalation?.gate}) — see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md\n`);
   354	      return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   355	    }
   356	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) {
   357	      io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: the run is parked — ${state.parkReason ?? 'no reason recorded'} (resume with: baton loop resume)\n`);
   358	      return EXIT_PARKED;
   359	    }
   360	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) {
   361	      io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: awaiting smoke approval — resume with: baton loop run --approve-smoke <token from ${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json>\n`);
   362	      return 0;
   363	    }
   364	
   365	    // ---- The phase loop. ---------------------------------------------------
   366	    while (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING && state.phaseIndex < state.phaseCount) {
   367	      const phase = spec.phases[state.phaseIndex];
   368	      const cap = spec.budgets.iterationCap;
   369	      let findings = '';
   370	      let failoverAttempt = 0;
   371	      /** @type {any | null} */
   372	      let forcedAssignment = null;
   373	      /** @type {string | null} */
   374	      let forcedPrompt = null;
   375	      let phaseDone = false;
   376	
   377	      while (!phaseDone) {
   378	        // The cap gates the SPAWN: at the cap the reducer escalates and a
   379	        // 6th child never starts.
   380	        if ((state.iterations?.[phase.id] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   381	          // ESCALATE persists at ANY spec cap — GATE_ITERATION only flips the
   382	          // status at the reducer's hard 5-cap (dogfood finding D7).
   383	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.ESCALATE, gate: phase.id });
   384	          atomicWriteText(
   385	            io.fs,
   386	            `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`,
   387	            `# Loop escalation\n\nGate '${phase.id}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap on run ${runId}.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n\nEscalation is operator-only: review and resolve the findings with the operator before any new gate attempt.\n`,
   388	          );
   389	          io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: gate '${phase.id}' hit the ${cap}-iteration cap — escalated (see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md)\n`);
   390	          return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   391	        }
   392	        if (childSeq >= spec.budgets.maxChildrenPerPhase * spec.phases.length) {
   393	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: 'total child budget exhausted' });
   394	          return EXIT_PARKED;
   395	        }
   396	
   397	        const resolved =
   398	          forcedAssignment ??
   399	          (() => {
   400	            const r = resolveRoles({ config, to: 'claude-code', avoid, avoidEntries, probes: null }).assignments[phase.role];
   401	            return r && r.mode !== 'unavailable' ? r : null;
   402	          })();
   403	        if (!resolved) {
   404	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: `no eligible platform/model for role '${phase.role}'` });
   405	          io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: no eligible assignment for role '${phase.role}' — parked\n`);
   406	          return EXIT_PARKED;
   407	        }
   408	        const assignment = { ...resolved, role: phase.role };
   409	        const prompt =
   410	          forcedPrompt ??
   411	          [
   412	            `You are the ${phase.role} for loop run ${runId}, phase '${phase.id}'.`,
   413	            `Goal: ${spec.goal}`,
   414	            spec.constraints.length > 0 ? `Constraints:\n${spec.constraints.map((/** @type {string} */ c) => `- ${c}`).join('\n')}` : '',
   415	            findings ? `The previous attempt was BLOCKED with these findings — address every one:\n${findings}` : '',
   416	            "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   417	          ]
   418	            .filter(Boolean)
   419	            .join('\n\n');
   420	        forcedAssignment = null;
   421	        forcedPrompt = null;
   422	
   423	        childSeq += 1;
   424	        const childId = `${String(childSeq).padStart(3, '0')}-${phase.id}`;
   425	        const logPath = `${p.dir}/children/${childId}.log`;
   426	        ensureDir(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children`);
   427	        const childSpec = buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, { root });
   428	        const result = await runner(childSpec, {
   429	          timeoutMs: spec.budgets.perRoleTimeoutMin * 60_000,
   430	          graceMs: 10_000,
   431	          logPath,
   432	          maxLogBytes: 1_000_000,
   433	          platform: assignment.platform,
   434	          // Persist the child's process group the INSTANT it spawns — a
   435	          // supervisor crash must leave every in-flight child reap-able by
   436	          // the reclaiming run (G4).
   437	          onStart: (/** @type {{pid: number, pgid: number}} */ info) => {
   438	            appendEntry(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`, { childId, pid: info.pid, pgid: info.pgid, startedAt: io.now() });
   439	          },
   440	        });
   441	        // Retire the child the moment it resolves — a reclaim must never kill
   442	        // a completed child's (possibly OS-recycled) process group (H3).
   443	        appendEntry(io.fs, `${p.dir}/children.ndjson`, { childId, endedAt: io.now() });
   444	
   445	        // Classification reads the child's LOG (the frozen transcript), so a
   446	        // limit banner routes to failover even when a verdict parsed.
   447	        const transcript = io.fs.existsSync(logPath) ? io.fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf8') : '';
   448	        const cls = classify({ text: transcriptTail(transcript), exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 0, platform: assignment.platform, table }).class;
   449	
   450	        if (cls === 'usage-limit' || cls === 'model-unavailable' || cls === 'other-error' || cls === 'throttle' || cls === 'auth') {
   451	          failoverAttempt += 1;
   452	          const decision = await runFailover({
   453	            root,
   454	            io,
   455	            config,
   456	            role: phase.role,
   457	            assignment,
   458	            transcript,
   459	            exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 1,
   460	            sessionHint,
   461	            probes: null,
   462	            avoid,
   463	            avoidEntries,
   464	            attempt: failoverAttempt,
   465	            loopState: { runId, phaseIndex: state.phaseIndex, iterations: state.iterations, status: state.status },
   466	          });
   467	          if (decision.action === 'park') {
   468	            await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PARK, reason: decision.reason });
   469	            io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: parked — ${decision.reason}${'resumeAt' in decision && decision.resumeAt ? ` (resume around ${decision.resumeAt})` : ''}\n`);
   470	            return EXIT_PARKED;
   471	          }
   472	          if (decision.action === 'relaunch') {
   473	            // Platform avoidance is PER-DEATH, not cumulative: runFailover
   474	            // already avoided the just-died platform when it resolved the
   475	            // relaunch. Accumulating here would exhaust every platform on a
   476	            // chained A→B→A failover and park instead of returning to A
   477	            // (acceptance constraint 2). Entry-level avoidance (dead MODELS)
   478	            // does accumulate — a rejected model stays rejected.
   479	            if (Array.isArray(decision.avoidEntries)) avoidEntries = decision.avoidEntries;
   480	            forcedAssignment = { ...decision.assignment, role: phase.role };
   481	            forcedPrompt = typeof decision.prompt === 'string' && decision.prompt.length > 0 ? decision.prompt : null;
   482	            continue; // relaunch the same phase on the new assignment
   483	          }
   484	          continue; // retry: re-spawn the same phase once more
   485	        }
   486	
   487	        const verdict = String(result.verdict ?? 'BLOCKED');
   488	        if (verdict === 'APPROVED' || verdict === 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   489	          await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE });
   490	          phaseDone = true;
   491	
   492	          // The smoke gate fires right after the smoke-build phase completes.
   493	          if (phase.id === 'smoke-build' && typeof spec.smoke?.cmd === 'string' && spec.smoke.cmd.length > 0) {
   494	            const [cmd, ...cmdArgs] = spec.smoke.cmd.split(/\s+/);
   495	            let smokeOut = '';
   496	            try {
   497	              const r = await io.execFile(cmd, cmdArgs, { cwd: root });
   498	              smokeOut = `${r?.stdout ?? ''}${r?.stderr ?? ''}`;
   499	            } catch (err) {
   500	              smokeOut = `smoke command failed: ${/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err)}`;
   501	            }
   502	            await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_AWAIT });
   503	            const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   504	            const inputs = {
   505	              stateDigest: dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(p.state, 'utf8')),
   506	              smokeCmd: spec.smoke.cmd,
   507	              smokeOutputDigest: dedupeKey(smokeOut),
   508	              gitHead: gitHeadOf(git),
   509	              gitContentDigest: gitContentOf(git),
   510	              childAssignment: JSON.stringify({ platform: assignment.platform, model: assignment.model }),
   511	            };
   512	            const token = smokeApprovalToken(inputs);
   513	            atomicWriteJson(io.fs, `${p.dir}/smoke-approval.json`, { token, inputs, issuedAt: io.now() });
   514	            atomicWriteText(
   515	              io.fs,
   516	              `${p.dir}/SMOKE-REVIEW.md`,
   517	              `# Smoke gate — human approval required\n\nRun: ${runId}\nCommand: \`${spec.smoke.cmd}\`\nExpected: ${spec.smoke.expect ?? '(unspecified)'}\n\n## Output\n\n\`\`\`\n${smokeOut}\n\`\`\`\n\nApprove with:\n\n    baton loop run --approve-smoke ${token}\n\nThe token is bound to the current state/output/git — any drift refuses it.\n`,
   518	            );
   519	            io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: smoke gate reached — review ${p.dir}/SMOKE-REVIEW.md and approve with --approve-smoke <token>\n`);
   520	            return 0;
   521	          }
   522	        } else {
   523	          // BLOCKED (or unparseable, already coerced to BLOCKED upstream).
   524	          findings = String(result.findings ?? '');
   525	          const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate: phase.id, verdict });
   526	          if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) {
   527	            atomicWriteText(
   528	              io.fs,
   529	              `${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md`,
   530	              `# Loop escalation\n\nGate '${phase.id}' exhausted its ${cap}-iteration cap on run ${runId}.\nLast findings:\n\n${findings}\n`,
   531	            );
   532	            io.stderr.write(`baton loop run: gate '${phase.id}' escalated at the cap — see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md\n`);
   533	            return EXIT_ESCALATED;
   534	          }
   535	        }
   536	      }
   537	    }
   538	
   539	    if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.DONE || state.phaseIndex >= state.phaseCount) {
   540	      io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: done — every phase completed (run ${runId})\n`);
   541	      return 0;
   542	    }
   543	    io.stdout.write(`baton loop run: stopped in status ${state.status}\n`);
   544	    return state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED ? EXIT_PARKED : state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED ? EXIT_ESCALATED : 0;
   545	  } finally {
   546	    // The lock is per-invocation: release on every exit path so a paused run
   547	    // (awaiting approval) can be resumed by the next invocation.
   548	    lock.release();
   549	  }
   550	}

    42	/**
    43	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    44	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    45	 */
    46	export async function cmdPipeline(args, io) {
    47	  /** @type {string[]} */
    48	  const positionals = [];
    49	  /** @type {string[]} */
    50	  const flagTokens = [];
    51	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    52	    const a = args[i];
    53	    if (typeof a === 'string' && a.startsWith('--')) {
    54	      flagTokens.push(a);
    55	      if (STRING_FLAGS.has(a.slice(2)) && i + 1 < args.length) {
    56	        i += 1;
    57	        flagTokens.push(args[i]);
    58	      }
    59	    } else {
    60	      positionals.push(a);
    61	    }
    62	  }
    63	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(flagTokens, {});
    64	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'pipeline', parsed.error);
    65	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    66	
    67	  const sub = positionals[0];
    68	  if (sub === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', 'a subcommand is required — try: baton pipeline run');
    69	  if (sub !== 'run' && sub !== 'resume') return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `unknown subcommand '${sub}' (supported: run, resume)`);
    70	  if (positionals.length > 1) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `unexpected argument '${positionals[1]}'`);
    71	  if (sub === 'resume') flags.__resume = true;
    72	
    73	  return runPipeline(flags, io);
    74	}

    76	/** Validate the spec's subtasks — every rejection names its offender.
    77	 * @param {any} subtasks @returns {string | null} */
    78	function validateSubtasks(subtasks) {
    79	  if (!Array.isArray(subtasks) || subtasks.length === 0) {
    80	    return 'loop.json needs a non-empty `subtasks` array ([{id, title}]) for a pipeline run';
    81	  }
    82	  const seen = new Set();
    83	  for (let i = 0; i < subtasks.length; i += 1) {
    84	    const st = subtasks[i];
    85	    if (typeof st?.id !== 'string' || st.id.length === 0) return `subtasks[${i}] is missing a string id`;
    86	    if (typeof st?.title !== 'string' || st.title.length === 0) return `subtasks[${i}] ('${st.id}') is missing a string title`;
    87	    if (seen.has(st.id)) return `subtasks carry a duplicate id '${st.id}' — ids name branches and must be unique`;
    88	    seen.add(st.id);
    89	  }
    90	  return null;
    91	}

    93	/**
    94	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags @param {any} io
    95	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    96	 */
    97	async function runPipeline(flags, io) {
    98	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    99	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   100	
   101	  const rawSpec = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${root}/loop.json`);
   102	  if (!rawSpec.ok) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `no loop.json at ${root} — scaffold one with: baton loop init "<goal>"`);
   103	  const spec = rawSpec.value;
   104	  const subtaskError = validateSubtasks(spec?.subtasks);
   105	  if (subtaskError !== null) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', subtaskError);
   106	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   107	  if (!config) return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `no readable baton.config.json at ${root} — the role matrix is required`);
   108	  // The 5-iteration cap is a hard invariant (Gate-2 fold G2): a spec asking
   109	  // for more is rejected BEFORE anything spawns.
   110	  const rawCap = spec?.budgets?.iterationCap;
   111	  if (rawCap !== undefined && (typeof rawCap !== 'number' || rawCap < 1 || rawCap > 5)) {
   112	    return usageError(io, flags, 'pipeline', `budgets.iterationCap must be a number between 1 and 5 (the 5-iteration cap is a hard invariant; got ${JSON.stringify(rawCap)})`);
   113	  }
   114	  const cap = typeof rawCap === 'number' ? rawCap : 5;
   115	  const timeoutMs = (typeof spec?.budgets?.perRoleTimeoutMin === 'number' ? spec.budgets.perRoleTimeoutMin : 30) * 60_000;
   116	
   117	  // One supervisor at a time — the same atomic run lock as `loop run`, with
   118	  // dead-owner reclaim + orphan reaping (Gate-2 fold G2/B8).
   119	  const lock = await acquireSupervisorLock(root, io, 'pipeline run');
   120	  if (lock.ok !== true) return lock.code;
   121	  try {
   122	    return await drivePipeline(flags, io, { root, p, spec, config, cap, timeoutMs });
   123	  } finally {
   124	    lock.release();
   125	  }
   126	}

   375	      for (;;) {

   377	        if (!resolved) return { parked: await park(`no eligible ${c.roleLabel} remains for subtask '${c.subtaskId}' (every chain entry is avoided)`) };

   382	        const cls = classify({ text: transcriptTail(log), exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 0, platform: asg.platform, table }).class;
   383	        if (cls === 'ok') return { result };

   389	          root,
   390	          io,
   391	          config,
   392	          role: c.roleChain,
   393	          assignment: asg,
   394	          transcript: log,
   395	          exitCode: result.exitCode ?? 1,
   396	          sessionHint: state.runId,
   397	          probes: null,
   398	          avoid: [],
   399	          avoidEntries: subtaskAvoidEntries,
   400	          attempt,
   401	          loopState: { runId: state.runId, phaseIndex: state.phaseIndex, iterations: state.iterations, status: state.status },
   402	        });
   403	        if (decision.action === 'park') return { parked: await park(`${c.roleLabel} failover parked subtask '${c.subtaskId}': ${decision.reason}`) };
   404	        if (decision.action === 'relaunch') {
   405	          if (Array.isArray(decision.avoidEntries)) subtaskAvoidEntries = decision.avoidEntries;
   406	          forced = { ...decision.assignment, role: c.childRole };
   407	        }
   408	      }
   409	    };
   410	
   411	    while (!merged) {
   412	      if ((state.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   413	        io.stderr.write(`baton pipeline run: gate '${gate}' hit the ${cap}-iteration cap — escalated (see ${p.dir}/ESCALATION.md)\n`);
   414	        return escalate(gate, findings, cap);
   415	      }
   416	
   417	      // Writer (write-capable, its own seat). Every resolution — including a
   418	      // plain BLOCKED retry — honors the subtask's avoided entries, so a
   419	      // model rejected earlier in this subtask is never re-picked (D4).
   420	      const resolvedWriter = forcedWriter ?? resolveOne(`worker-${seat}`, subtaskAvoidEntries);
   421	      if (!resolvedWriter) return park(`no eligible writer remains for subtask '${st.id}' (every chain entry is avoided)`);
   422	      const writerAsg = { ...resolvedWriter, role: `worker-${seat}` };
   423	      forcedWriter = null;
   424	      const writerPrompt = [
   425	        `You are the writer (worker-${seat}) for subtask '${st.id}': ${st.title}.`,
   426	        `Goal: ${spec.goal}. Work ONLY on branch ${branch} in your worktree; commit your work there.`,
   427	        findings ? `The previous attempt was BLOCKED — address every finding:\n${findings}` : '',
   428	        "When your work is committed and self-checked, End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   429	      ]
   430	        .filter(Boolean)
   431	        .join('\n\n');
   432	      const writerResult = await spawn(writerAsg, writerPrompt, seats[seat], `${st.id}-writer`);
   433	
   434	      // The writer's result is CONSUMED, never discarded (Gate-2 fold G3):
   435	      // classify its log first — a limit/model death routes through failover,
   436	      // a BLOCKED self-check retries the writer, and only a passing writer
   437	      // hands off to review.
   438	      const writerLog = writerResult.logPath && io.fs.existsSync(writerResult.logPath) ? io.fs.readFileSync(writerResult.logPath, 'utf8') : '';
   439	      const writerCls = classify({ text: transcriptTail(writerLog), exitCode: writerResult.exitCode ?? 0, platform: writerAsg.platform, table }).class;
   440	      if (writerCls !== 'ok') {
   441	        failoverAttempt += 1;
   442	        // Failover is BOUNDED: at most one relaunch per configured chain entry
   443	        // for this seat — beyond that the subtask parks instead of ping-ponging
   444	        // across platforms forever (H2).
   445	        const chainLen = Array.isArray(config?.roles?.[`worker-${seat}`]) ? config.roles[`worker-${seat}`].length : 1;
   446	        if (failoverAttempt > chainLen) {
   447	          return park(`subtask '${st.id}' exhausted its failover budget (${chainLen} chain entr${chainLen === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'}, ${failoverAttempt} deaths) — parked instead of looping`);
   448	        }
   449	        const decision = await runFailover({
   450	          root,
   451	          io,
   452	          config,
   453	          role: `worker-${seat}`,
   454	          assignment: writerAsg,
   455	          transcript: writerLog,
   456	          exitCode: writerResult.exitCode ?? 1,
   457	          sessionHint: state.runId,
   458	          probes: null,
   459	          avoid: [],
   460	          avoidEntries: subtaskAvoidEntries,
   461	          attempt: failoverAttempt,
   462	          loopState: { runId: state.runId, phaseIndex: state.phaseIndex, iterations: state.iterations, status: state.status },
   463	        });
   464	        if (decision.action === 'park') return park(`writer failover parked subtask '${st.id}': ${decision.reason}`);
   465	        if (decision.action === 'relaunch') {
   466	          // Carry entry-level avoidance across relaunches — a rejected model
   467	          // stays rejected for this subtask (H2).
   468	          if (Array.isArray(decision.avoidEntries)) subtaskAvoidEntries = decision.avoidEntries;
   469	          forcedWriter = { ...decision.assignment, role: `worker-${seat}` };
   470	        }
   471	        continue; // relaunch or retry the writer — never review a failed attempt
   472	      }
   473	      if (writerResult.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && writerResult.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   474	        findings = String(writerResult.findings ?? '');
   475	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   476	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED || (after.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   477	          return escalate(gate, findings, cap);
   478	        }
   479	        continue; // the writer retries; no reviewer sees a failed attempt
   480	      }
   481	
   482	      const post = await postflightWorktree(root, { seat, branch, mainSha }, io);
   483	      if (post.ok !== true) return park(`postflight refused subtask '${st.id}': ${post.refusal}`);
   484	
   485	      // An empty branch never merges (Gate-2 fold G3): the writer must have
   486	      // actually committed work ahead of main.
   487	      const ahead = String((await io.execFile('git', ['log', `main..${branch}`, '--format=%H'], { cwd: root })).stdout).trim();
   488	      if (ahead.length === 0) return park(`subtask '${st.id}' produced an EMPTY branch (no commits ahead of main) — nothing to review or merge`);
   489	
   490	      // Reviewer-seat preflight (Gate-2 fold G5): the reviewing seat must be
   491	      // listed and clean before a reviewer spawns into it.
   492	      try {
   493	        const otherBranch = String((await withSeatHealing(other, () => io.execFile('git', ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'], { cwd: seats[other] }))).stdout).trim();
   494	        const reviewerPre = await preflightWorktree(root, { seat: other, branch: otherBranch }, io);
   495	        if (reviewerPre.ok !== true) return park(`reviewer-seat preflight refused subtask '${st.id}': ${reviewerPre.refusal}`);
   496	      } catch (err) {
   497	        return park(`reviewer-seat preparation failed for subtask '${st.id}': ${String(/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? err).split('\n')[0]}`);
   498	      }
   499	
   500	      // Reviewer (read-only, the OTHER seat's model and cwd, subtask-reviewer role).
   501	      const reviewPrompt = [
   502	        `You are the subtask-reviewer for subtask '${st.id}': ${st.title}.`,
   503	        `Review the change on ${branch} against main from the ${other} seat (fresh context). Run: git diff main..${branch} (and git log main..${branch}) to see exactly what changed — branch refs are shared across worktrees.`,
   504	        "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   505	      ].join('\n\n');
   506	      // A reviewer DEATH is never a review verdict (dogfood finding D6): a
   507	      // failure-class result re-resolves the role (entry avoidance carried on
   508	      // subtaskAvoidEntries) and relaunches, bounded by the chain length —
   509	      // only a real verdict reaches the gate.
   510	      const review = await superviseVerdictChild({
   511	        roleChain: `worker-${other}`,
   512	        childRole: 'subtask-reviewer',
   513	        prompt: reviewPrompt,
   514	        seatPath: seats[other],
   515	        label: `${st.id}-review`,
   516	        subtaskId: st.id,
   517	        roleLabel: 'reviewer',
   518	      });
   519	      if (review.parked !== undefined) return review.parked;
   520	      if (review.result.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && review.result.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   521	        findings = String(review.result.findings ?? '');
   522	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   523	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED || (after.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   524	          return escalate(gate, findings, cap);
   525	        }
   526	        continue;
   527	      }
   528	
   529	      // Merger (read-only child — it re-checks; the SUPERVISOR merges).
   530	      const mergerPrompt = [
   531	        `You are the merger for subtask '${st.id}'. Adversarially re-check ${branch} against main before it merges.`,
   532	        "End with exactly:\nVERDICT: APPROVED | APPROVED_WITH_NOTES | BLOCKED\nFINDINGS: numbered findings, or 'none'",
   533	      ].join('\n\n');
   534	      const mergerCheck = await superviseVerdictChild({
   535	        roleChain: 'merger',
   536	        childRole: 'merger',
   537	        prompt: mergerPrompt,
   538	        seatPath: root,
   539	        label: `${st.id}-merge-check`,
   540	        subtaskId: st.id,
   541	        roleLabel: 'merger',
   542	      });
   543	      if (mergerCheck.parked !== undefined) return mergerCheck.parked;
   544	      if (mergerCheck.result.verdict !== 'APPROVED' && mergerCheck.result.verdict !== 'APPROVED_WITH_NOTES') {
   545	        findings = String(mergerCheck.result.findings ?? '');
   546	        const after = await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION, gate, verdict: 'BLOCKED' });
   547	        if (after.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED || (after.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0) >= cap) {
   548	          return escalate(gate, findings, cap);
   549	        }
   550	        continue;
   551	      }
   552	
   553	      const merge = await mergeSubtask(root, { branch }, io);
   554	      if (merge.ok !== true) return park(`merge of '${branch}' refused: ${merge.reason}`);
   555	      // The receipt lands BEFORE the phase-advance journal write (I1): a
   556	      // crash between the two resumes into a receipt-backed advance.
   557	      appendEntry(io.fs, mergesPath, { subtaskId: st.id, branch, mergedAt: io.now() });
   558	      merged = true;
   559	    }
   560	
   561	    await transition({ type: LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE });
   562	  }
   563	
   564	  if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { status: state.status, subtasks: subtasks.length } });
   565	  else io.stdout.write(`baton pipeline run: done — ${subtasks.length} subtask(s) merged\n`);
   566	  return state.status === LOOP_STATUS.DONE ? 0 : state.status === LOOP_STATUS.PARKED ? EXIT_PARKED : 0;
   567	}

    15	/** The frozen status vocabulary. */
    16	export const LOOP_STATUS = Object.freeze({
    17	  RUNNING: 'running',
    18	  AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL: 'awaiting-smoke-approval',

    26	  PHASE_ADVANCE: 'phase-advance',
    27	  GATE_ITERATION: 'gate-iteration',
    28	  ESCALATE: 'escalate',
    29	  PARK: 'park',

    35	// Every gate loops at most 5 times — a repo-wide hard invariant (AGENTS.md
    36	// §Review gates); the reducer refuses a 6th and escalates instead.
    37	const GATE_ITERATION_CAP = 5;
    38	
    39	/** @param {string} root */
    40	export function loopPaths(root) {
    41	  const dir = `${root}/.handoff/loop`;
    42	  return { dir, state: `${dir}/state.json`, journal: `${dir}/journal.ndjson` };
    43	}

    45	/**
    46	 * Fresh run state — pure and deterministic from the injected io (identity
    47	 * facts + clock only; no Date.now/Math.random, which would break replay).
    48	 * @param {any} spec a VALIDATED loop spec @param {any} io
    49	 */
    50	export function initLoopState(spec, io) {
    51	  const runId = `loop-${dedupeKey({ host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime, at: io.now() }).slice(0, 12)}`;
    52	  /** @type {Record<string, number>} */
    53	  const iterations = {};
    54	  for (const p of spec.phases ?? []) {
    55	    if (/gate/.test(String(p.id))) iterations[p.id] = 0;
    56	  }
    57	  return {
    58	    schema: LOOP_STATE_SCHEMA,
    59	    runId,
    60	    goal: spec.goal,
    61	    phaseCount: Array.isArray(spec.phases) ? spec.phases.length : 0,
    62	    phaseIndex: 0,
    63	    iterations,
    64	    status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING,
    65	    parkReason: null,
    66	    escalation: null,
    67	    smokeApproval: null,
    68	    createdAt: io.now(),
    69	    journalSeq: 0,
    70	  };
    71	}
    72	
    73	/**
    74	 * The pure transition reducer. Never mutates its input; unknown events and
    75	 * refused transitions return the input state unchanged (a new reference is
    76	 * only produced for a real transition).
    77	 * @param {any} state @param {any} ev
    78	 */
    79	export function applyLoopEvent(state, ev) {
    80	  switch (ev?.type) {
    81	    case LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE: {
    82	      const next = state.phaseIndex + 1;
    83	      if (next >= state.phaseCount) return { ...state, phaseIndex: state.phaseCount, status: LOOP_STATUS.DONE };
    84	      return { ...state, phaseIndex: next };
    85	    }
    86	    case LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION: {
    87	      const gate = String(ev.gate);
    88	      const current = state.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0;
    89	      // The 6th attempt is REFUSED: the counter stays at the cap and the run
    90	      // escalates with a record naming the gate — never a 6th run.
    91	      if (current >= GATE_ITERATION_CAP) {
    92	        return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED, escalation: { gate, iteration: current } };
    93	      }
    94	      return { ...state, iterations: { ...state.iterations, [gate]: current + 1 } };
    95	    }
    96	    case LOOP_EVENT.ESCALATE: {
    97	      // Supervisors enforce spec caps LOWER than the hard invariant; this
    98	      // event persists that escalation (dogfood finding D7: a cap-3 pipeline
    99	      // exit left state.json 'running' because only the reducer's own 5-cap
   100	      // could flip the status). Idempotent — an already-escalated run keeps
   101	      // its original record.
   102	      if (state.status === LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED) return state;
   103	      const gate = String(ev.gate);
   104	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED, escalation: { gate, iteration: state.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0 } };
   105	    }
   106	    case LOOP_EVENT.PARK:
   107	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.PARKED, parkReason: ev.reason ?? null };
   108	    case LOOP_EVENT.RESUME:
   109	      // Only a PARK is resumable; an escalation is an operator decision.
   110	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) return state;
   111	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING, parkReason: null };
   112	    case LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_AWAIT:
   113	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL };
   114	    case LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_APPROVE: {
   115	      // Guarded transition: only meaningful while awaiting, and only with the
   116	      // caller's verifySmokeToken result stamped verified === true. A missing
   117	      // or false `verified` is unverified — it never resumes the run.
   118	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) return state;
   119	      if (ev.verified !== true) return state;
   120	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING, smokeApproval: { token: ev.token, at: ev.ts ?? null } };
   121	    }
   122	    default:
   123	      return state;
   124	  }
   125	}

   127	/**
   128	 * Atomic snapshot write (tmp + rename under .handoff/loop).

   131	export async function writeLoopState(root, state, io) {

   137	/**
   138	 * Append one journal event; allocates the next seq past
   139	 * max(snapshot.journalSeq, journal tail) unless the entry carries one.
   140	 * @param {string} root @param {any} ev @param {any} io
   141	 * @returns {Promise<number>} the persisted seq

   143	export async function appendLoopEvent(root, ev, io) {
   144	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   145	  ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   146	  let seq = ev.seq;
   147	  if (typeof seq !== 'number') {
   148	    const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.state);

   152	      for (const e of readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal).entries) {
   153	        if (typeof e.seq === 'number' && e.seq > tailSeq) tailSeq = e.seq;
   154	      }
   155	    }
   156	    seq = Math.max(snapSeq, tailSeq) + 1;
   157	  }

   164	  };

   167	}

   169	/**
   170	 * Load = snapshot + torn-tail-tolerant replay of journal events PAST the
   171	 * snapshot's seq. Duplicate seqs/dedupeKeys apply exactly once, so a
   172	 * supervisor-death recovery never re-runs a completed iteration.
   173	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io
   174	 * @returns {Promise<{state: any, warnings: string[]}>}
   175	 */
   176	export async function loadLoopState(root, io) {
   177	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   178	  /** @type {string[]} */
   179	  const warnings = [];
   180	  const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.state);
   181	  if (!snap.ok) return { state: null, warnings: ['no loop state snapshot found'] };
   182	  let state = snap.value;
   183	  const baseSeq = typeof state.journalSeq === 'number' ? state.journalSeq : 0;
   184	
   185	  if (io.fs.existsSync(p.journal)) {
   186	    const { entries, warnings: jw } = readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal);
   187	    for (const w of jw ?? []) warnings.push(`journal: ${w.kind ?? 'warning'} at line ${w.line ?? '?'}`);
   188	    const applied = new Set();
   189	    let maxSeq = baseSeq;
   190	    for (const e of entries) {
   191	      const seq = typeof e.seq === 'number' ? e.seq : null;
   192	      if (seq !== null && seq <= baseSeq) continue; // already folded into the snapshot
   193	      const key = e.dedupeKey ?? (seq !== null ? `seq:${seq}` : null);
   194	      if (key !== null && applied.has(key)) continue; // replayed duplicate — apply once
   195	      if (seq !== null && applied.has(`seq:${seq}`)) continue;
   196	      state = applyLoopEvent(state, e);
   197	      if (key !== null) applied.add(key);
   198	      if (seq !== null) {
   199	        applied.add(`seq:${seq}`);
   200	        if (seq > maxSeq) maxSeq = seq;
   201	      }
   202	    }
   203	    state = { ...state, journalSeq: maxSeq };
   204	  }
   205	  return { state, warnings };
   206	}

   208	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   209	// Smoke-approval token — a STRUCTURED digest over the six bound inputs, so a
   210	// stale approval is refused NAMING what moved (mirrors the receive receipt
   211	// token's driftedInputs discipline).
   212	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   213	
   214	const SMOKE_TOKEN_PREFIX = 'smk1';
   215	const SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS = /** @type {const} */ ([
   216	  'stateDigest',
   217	  'smokeCmd',
   218	  'smokeOutputDigest',
   219	  'gitHead',
   220	  'gitContentDigest',
   221	  'childAssignment',
   222	]);
   223	
   224	/**
   225	 * Deterministic structured token. Per-field digests keep field boundaries
   226	 * (no concatenation collisions) and let verification name drifted inputs.
   227	 * Missing bound fields throw — a token over partial inputs is meaningless.
   228	 * @param {Record<string, string>} inputs
   229	 * @returns {string}
   230	 */
   231	export function smokeApprovalToken(inputs) {
   232	  for (const f of SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS) {
   233	    if (typeof inputs?.[f] !== 'string') throw new Error(`smoke approval token: required input '${f}' is missing`);
   234	  }
   235	  return `${SMOKE_TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.map((f) => dedupeKey(inputs[f]).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
   236	}
   237	
   238	/**
   239	 * Recompute against current inputs; positional comparison names every
   240	 * drifted input. Never throws — partial current inputs simply cannot verify.
   241	 * @param {string} presented @param {Record<string, string>} inputs
   242	 * @returns {{ok: true} | {ok: false, driftedInputs: string[]}}
   243	 */
   244	export function verifySmokeToken(presented, inputs) {
   245	  /** @type {string} */
   246	  let current;
   247	  try {
   248	    current = smokeApprovalToken(inputs);
   249	  } catch {
   250	    return { ok: false, driftedInputs: SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((f) => typeof inputs?.[f] !== 'string') };
   251	  }
   252	  if (presented === current) return { ok: true };
   253	  const a = String(presented ?? '').split('.');
   254	  const b = current.split('.');
   255	  /** @type {string[]} */
   256	  const drifted = [];
   257	  SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.forEach((f, i) => {
   258	    if (a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]) drifted.push(f);
   259	  });
   260	  return { ok: false, driftedInputs: drifted.length > 0 ? drifted : [...SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS] };
   261	}

    29	/**
    30	 * Assemble the spawn contract for a role child. Reviewers are read-only on
    31	 * every platform; every child is marked supervised (its own baton hooks
    32	 * no-op), carries the sole-author git identity, and has stdin CLOSED at
    33	 * spawn (the codex-exec stdin-hang field failure).
    34	 * @param {{platform: string, role: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string}} assignment
    35	 * @param {string} prompt
    36	 * @param {{root: string, gitDir?: string}} opts
    37	 * @returns {{command: string, args: string[], env: Record<string, string>, stdio: any[], cwd: string}}
    38	 */
    39	export function buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, opts) {
    40	  const readOnly = REVIEWER_ROLES.has(assignment.role);
    41	  const env = { BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD: '1', ...GIT_IDENTITY };
    42	  const stdio = ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'];
    43	
    44	  if (assignment.platform === 'claude-code') {

    48	    const args = ['-p', prompt, '--model', assignment.model, '--output-format', 'json'];
    49	    if (readOnly) {
    50	      // Scoped read-only git so a reviewer can actually SEE the diff it
    51	      // reviews — still no write/edit capability.
    52	      args.push('--permission-mode', 'default', '--allowedTools', 'Read,Grep,Glob,Bash(git diff:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(git show:*)');
    53	    } else {
    54	      args.push('--permission-mode', 'acceptEdits', '--allowedTools', 'Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Bash');
    55	    }
    56	    return { command: 'claude', args, env, stdio, cwd: opts.root };
    57	  }
    58	
    59	  // codex (and the default shape for exec-style CLIs).
    60	  const args = ['exec', '-C', opts.root, '-s', readOnly ? 'read-only' : 'workspace-write', '--model', assignment.model];
    61	  if (assignment.effort) args.push('-c', `model_reasoning_effort=${assignment.effort}`);

    64	    // outside the seat-cwd sandbox. Without this grant a codex writer can

    67	    args.push('-c', `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[${JSON.stringify(opts.gitDir)}]`);
    68	  }
    69	  args.push(prompt);
    70	  return { command: 'codex', args, env, stdio, cwd: opts.root };
    71	}
