    73	const VERDICT_RE = /VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|APPROVED|BLOCKED)\b/g;
    74	
    75	/** @param {string} region @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string} | null} */
    76	function lastVerdictIn(region) {
    77	  let last = null;
    78	  for (const m of region.matchAll(VERDICT_RE)) last = m;
    79	  if (!last) return null;
    80	  const after = region.slice((last.index ?? 0) + last[0].length);
    81	  return { verdict: last[1], findings: after.trim() };
    82	}
    83	
    84	/**
    85	 * Region-bounded verdict parsing — the prompt region (which quotes the
    86	 * verdict format in its instructions) is NEVER scanned, and there is no
    87	 * whole-transcript fallback. Unparseable is BLOCKED, never APPROVED.
    88	 * - codex: only the text after the LAST line starting with 'tokens used'.
    89	 * - claude-code: only the `result` field of the structured JSON output.
    90	 * Multiple tails inside the trusted region → the LAST one wins.
    91	 * @param {string} transcript @param {{platform: string}} opts
    92	 * @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string, reason?: string}}
    93	 */
    94	export function parseVerdict(transcript, { platform }) {
    95	  const unparseable = { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: '', reason: 'unparseable' };
    96	  const text = String(transcript ?? '');
    97	
    98	  if (platform === 'claude-code') {
    99	    let obj = null;
   100	    try {
   101	      obj = JSON.parse(text.trim());
   102	    } catch {
   103	      return unparseable;
   104	    }
   105	    if (typeof obj?.result !== 'string') return unparseable;
   106	    const hit = lastVerdictIn(obj.result);
   107	    return hit ?? unparseable;
   108	  }
   109	
   110	  // codex: locate the LAST 'tokens used' marker line; the trusted region is
   111	  // strictly after it.
   112	  const lines = text.split('\n');
   113	  let markerLine = -1;
   114	  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
   115	    if (/^tokens used\b/i.test(lines[i])) markerLine = i;
   116	  }
   117	  if (markerLine === -1) return unparseable;
   118	  const region = lines.slice(markerLine + 1).join('\n');
   119	  const hit = lastVerdictIn(region);
   120	  return hit ?? unparseable;
   121	}
   122	
   123	const TRUNCATION_MARKER = '\n[... truncated by baton log cap ...]\n';
   124	
   125	/**
   126	 * Cap a transcript: head preserved, middle replaced with a marker, TAIL
   127	 * preserved verbatim (the verdict lives at the end and must never be cut).
   128	 * @param {string} text @param {number} maxBytes
   129	 * @returns {string}
   130	 */
   131	export function capLog(text, maxBytes) {
   132	  const s = String(text ?? '');
   133	  if (Buffer.byteLength(s) <= maxBytes) return s;
   134	  const headBytes = Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxBytes * 0.4));
   135	  const tailBytes = Math.max(1, maxBytes - headBytes);
   136	  const buf = Buffer.from(s);
   137	  const head = buf.subarray(0, headBytes).toString();
   138	  const tail = buf.subarray(buf.length - tailBytes).toString();
   139	  return head + TRUNCATION_MARKER + tail;
   140	}
   141	
   142	/**
   143	 * Exit classification delegates to core detect — one classifier, one
   144	 * signature table, no drift. Returns exactly classify(...).class.
   145	 * @param {string} transcript @param {number} exitCode @param {string} platform @param {any} table
   146	 * @returns {string}
   147	 */
   148	export function classifyChildExit(transcript, exitCode, platform, table) {
   149	  return classify({ text: transcript, exitCode, platform, table }).class;
   150	}
   151	
   152	/** @param {number} pid @param {NodeJS.Signals} sig */
   153	function killGroup(pid, sig) {
   154	  try {
   155	    process.kill(-pid, sig);
   156	  } catch {
   157	    // ESRCH — already gone.
   158	  }
   159	}
   160	
   161	/**
   162	 * Spawn and supervise one child: detached in its OWN process group, stdin
   163	 * closed; on timeout SIGTERM the group, wait graceMs, SIGKILL the group (no
   164	 * zombie grandchildren). Output streams to a capped log at opts.logPath; the
   165	 * verdict is parsed from the full transcript, region-bounded.
   166	 * @param {{command: string, args: string[], env?: Record<string, string>, cwd?: string}} spec
   167	 * @param {{timeoutMs: number, graceMs: number, logPath: string, maxLogBytes?: number, platform?: string, onStart?: (info: {pid: number, pgid: number}) => void}} opts
   168	 * @returns {Promise<{timedOut: boolean, exitCode: number | null, verdict?: string, findings?: string, reason?: string, logPath: string, pgid?: number}>}
   169	 */
   170	export function superviseChild(spec, opts) {
   171	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
   172	    const maxLogBytes = opts.maxLogBytes ?? 1_000_000;
   173	    const child = spawn(spec.command, spec.args, {
   174	      cwd: spec.cwd,
   175	      env: { ...process.env, ...(spec.env ?? {}) },
   176	      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
   177	      detached: true, // its own process group — the kill unit
   178	    });
   179	
   180	    // Report the group at spawn time so the supervisor can persist it BEFORE
   181	    // the child completes — a supervisor crash leaves the orphan reap-able.
   182	    const pgid = typeof child.pid === 'number' ? child.pid : -1;
   183	    if (typeof opts.onStart === 'function' && typeof child.pid === 'number') {
   184	      opts.onStart({ pid: child.pid, pgid });
   185	    }
   186	
   187	    let out = '';
   188	    let timedOut = false;
   189	    /** @type {NodeJS.Timeout | null} */
   190	    let killTimer = null;
   191	
   192	    const onChunk = (/** @type {Buffer} */ c) => {
   193	      out += c.toString();
   194	    };
   195	    child.stdout?.on('data', onChunk);
   196	    child.stderr?.on('data', onChunk);
   197	
   198	    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
   199	      timedOut = true;
   200	      if (typeof child.pid === 'number') {
   201	        killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
   202	        killTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   203	          if (typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   204	        }, opts.graceMs);
   205	      }
   206	    }, opts.timeoutMs);
   207	
   208	    const finish = (/** @type {number | null} */ exitCode) => {
   209	      clearTimeout(timeout);
   210	      if (killTimer) clearTimeout(killTimer);
   211	      // Belt-and-braces: reap any group survivors even on a clean exit path.
   212	      if (timedOut && typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   213	      try {
   214	        mkdirSync(dirname(opts.logPath), { recursive: true });
   215	        writeFileSync(opts.logPath, capLog(out, maxLogBytes));
   216	      } catch {
   217	        // The log must never mask the result.
   218	      }
   219	      const parsed = parseVerdict(out, { platform: opts.platform ?? 'codex' });
   220	      resolve({
   221	        timedOut,
   222	        exitCode: timedOut ? null : exitCode,
   223	        verdict: parsed.verdict,
   224	        findings: parsed.findings,
   225	        ...(parsed.reason ? { reason: parsed.reason } : {}),
   226	        logPath: opts.logPath,
   227	        pgid,
   228	      });
   229	    };
   230	
   231	    child.on('error', () => finish(null));
   232	    child.on('close', (code) => finish(code));
   233	  });
   234	}

   239	  for (const chunk of chunks) {
   240	    if (TRAILER_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(chunk))) {
   241	      const sha = chunk.slice(0, chunk.indexOf(' '));
   242	      return {
   243	        id: 'git-guard',
   244	        ok: false,
   245	        detail: `commit ${sha} carries an AI attribution trailer — rewrite it before publishing (git rebase -i / git commit --amend)`,
   246	      };
   247	    }
   248	  }
   249	  return { id: 'git-guard', ok: true, detail: `no AI trailers in the last ${GUARD_COMMIT_BOUND} commits` };
   250	}
   251	
   252	/**
   253	 * `baton doctor` — machine health report: attribution settings, git-guard
   254	 * trailer scan, journal size, filesystem boundary, and per-platform probe
   255	 * records ({capability, outcome}, 3 s bound, 15-min cache). Report-only by
   256	 * default; `--strict` turns any failing check into exit 1.
   257	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
   258	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   259	 */
   260	export async function cmdDoctor(args, io) {
   261	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { strict: 'boolean' });
   262	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'doctor', parsed.error);
   263	  const flags = parsed.flags;
   264	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
   265	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
   266	  /** @type {{id: string, ok: boolean, detail?: string}[]} */
   267	  const checks = [];
   268	
   269	  // Attribution settings: repo-level first, then the user's global file.
   270	  const settingsText = readOrNull(io, `${root}/.claude/settings.json`) ?? readOrNull(io, `${io.env?.HOME ?? ''}/.claude/settings.json`);
   271	  let attrOk = false;
   272	  try {
   273	    const s = settingsText === null ? null : JSON.parse(settingsText);
   274	    attrOk = s?.attribution?.commit === '' && s?.attribution?.pr === '';
   275	  } catch {
   276	    attrOk = false;
   277	  }
   278	  checks.push({
   279	    id: 'attribution-settings',
   280	    ok: attrOk,
   281	    detail: attrOk ? 'attribution.commit and attribution.pr are ""' : 'set {"attribution":{"commit":"","pr":""}} in .claude/settings.json (baton init does this)',
   282	  });
   283	
   284	  checks.push(await gitGuardCheck(io, root));
   285	
   286	  // .handoff gitignore coverage (audit finding): doctor itself writes the
   287	  // probe cache into .handoff/log/, so running doctor BEFORE init in a clean
   288	  // repo leaves .handoff/ committable. Flag the gap whenever the tree exists
   289	  // without ignore coverage.
   290	  {
   291	    let handoffExists = false;
   292	    try {
   293	      handoffExists = io.fs.statSync(`${root}/.handoff`).isDirectory();
   294	    } catch {
   295	      handoffExists = false;
   296	    }
   297	    const covered = !ensureIgnoreLine(readOrNull(io, `${root}/.gitignore`), '.handoff/').changed;
   298	    checks.push({
   299	      id: 'handoff-ignored',
   300	      ok: !handoffExists || covered,
   301	      detail:
   302	        !handoffExists || covered
   303	          ? handoffExists
   304	            ? '.gitignore covers .handoff/'
   305	            : 'no .handoff/ tree yet'
   306	          : '.handoff/ exists but .gitignore does not cover it — run baton init (never commit .handoff/)',
   307	    });
   308	  }
   309	
   310	  const journalText = readOrNull(io, p.journal);
   311	  const journalBytes = journalText === null ? 0 : Buffer.byteLength(journalText);
   312	  checks.push({
   313	    id: 'journal-size',
   314	    ok: journalBytes <= JOURNAL_WARN_BYTES,
   315	    detail: journalBytes > JOURNAL_WARN_BYTES ? `journal is ${(journalBytes / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB (> 5 MB) — finalize to rotate it` : `${journalBytes} bytes`,
   316	  });
   317	
   318	
   319	  // Platform probes + version probes + mount detection: every non-git child
   320	  // invocation rides the same 15-min cache in the state dir.
   321	  const cachePath = `${p.logDir}/probe-cache.json`;
   322	  const cached = safeReadJson(io.fs, cachePath);
   323	  /** @type {any[]} */
   324	  let platforms;
   325	  /** @type {Record<string, string | null>} */
   326	  let versions;
   327	  /** @type {string | null} */
   328	  let mountSource;
   329	  if (cached.ok && typeof cached.value?.at === 'string' && Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(cached.value.at) < PROBE_CACHE_MS && Array.isArray(cached.value.records)) {
   330	    platforms = cached.value.records;
   331	    versions = cached.value.versions ?? {};
   332	    mountSource = cached.value.mount ?? null;
   333	  } else {
   334	    /** @type {any} */
   335	    let table = null;
   336	    try {
   337	      // Packaged data, not repo state: read through the real fs so probes can
   338	      // classify limit responses regardless of the injected io.fs contents.
   339	      table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, { fs: realFs });
   340	    } catch {
   341	      table = null;
   342	    }
   343	    platforms = [];
   344	    for (const probe of PROBES) platforms.push(await runProbe(probe, io, table));
   345	    versions = {};
   346	    for (const platform of Object.keys(VERSION_BINS)) versions[platform] = await versionOf(platform, io);
   347	    mountSource = null;
   348	    try {
   349	      const df = await io.execFile('df', ['-P', root], { timeout: 2000 });
   350	      mountSource = ((df.stdout ?? '').split('\n')[1] ?? '').trim().split(/\s+/)[0] || null;
   351	    } catch {
   352	      mountSource = null;
   353	    }
   354	    // Jail before writing the probe cache (iter-3 F4): the cache rides
   355	    // .handoff/log, so a symlinked .handoff or log dir must never redirect the
   356	    // write outside the repository (threat model). Diagnostics are best-effort —
   357	    // on an unsafe tree we simply skip caching; the atomic write already
   358	    // prevents a torn cache under concurrent doctors.
   359	    if (checkHandoffTree(root, io).ok) {
   360	      ensureDir(io.fs, p.logDir);
   361	      atomicWriteJson(io.fs, cachePath, { at: io.now(), records: platforms, versions, mount: mountSource });
   362	    }
   363	  }
   364	
   365	  // Network-filesystem detection (gate-2 major 13): a mount source that looks
   366	  // like SMB/NFS fails the check; unverifiable degrades to the static boundary.
   367	  if (mountSource === null) {
   368	    checks.push({
   369	      id: 'filesystem',
   370	      ok: true,
   371	      detail: 'mount type unverifiable — v1 supports local filesystems only; lock/rename atomicity is not guaranteed on network or cloud-sync mounts',
   372	    });
   373	  } else if (/^\/\/|@|^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+:\//.test(mountSource)) {
   374	    checks.push({
   375	      id: 'filesystem',
   376	      ok: false,
   377	      detail: `${mountSource} looks like a network mount — lock/rename atomicity is not guaranteed there; v1 supports local filesystems only`,
   378	    });
   379	  } else {
   380	    checks.push({ id: 'filesystem', ok: true, detail: `local mount (${mountSource}) — note: v1 supports local filesystems only` });
   381	  }
   382	
   383	  // Version floors + tested cap, and the hook trust/canary surfaces.
   384	  for (const platform of Object.keys(VERSION_BINS)) {
   385	    checks.push(versionCheck(platform, versions[platform] ?? null));
   386	  }
   387	  checks.push(hookSurfaceCheck(io, root, p, 'codex', '.codex/hooks.json', 'Stop', 'trust review may be pending (run /hooks inside Codex to trust the definitions)'));
   388	  checks.push(hookSurfaceCheck(io, root, p, 'cursor', '.cursor/hooks.json', 'stop', 'project hooks require a trusted workspace in Cursor'));
   389	
   390	  const failing = checks.filter((c) => !c.ok);
   391	  if (flags.json) {
   392	    emitEnvelope(io, { ok: failing.length === 0, data: { checks, platforms }, warnings: failing.map((c) => `${c.id}: ${c.detail ?? 'failed'}`) });
   393	  } else {
   394	    for (const c of checks) io.stdout.write(`${c.ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'} ${c.id}${c.detail ? ` — ${c.detail}` : ''}\n`);
   395	    for (const r of platforms) io.stdout.write(`probe ${r.platform}: capability ${r.capability ?? 'not-installed'}, outcome ${r.outcome}\n`);
   396	  }
   397	  return flags.strict === true && failing.length > 0 ? 1 : 0;
   398	}

    27	 * lstat walk (gate-2 fix 6): never follows links. The tree was jail-checked

    30	 * @param {any} io @param {string} dir @returns {string[]}

    32	function walk(io, dir) {
    33	  /** @type {string[]} */
    34	  const out = [];
    35	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(dir)) return out;

    59	}
    60	
    61	/** @param {any} io @param {string} path */
    62	function scrubLinesFile(io, path) {
    63	  const raw = io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    64	  let changed = false;
    65	  const lines = raw.split('\n').map((/** @type {string} */ line) => {
    66	    if (line.trim() === '') return line;
    67	    /** @type {any} */
    68	    let parsed;
    69	    try {
    70	      parsed = JSON.parse(line);
    71	    } catch {
    72	      return line; // tolerate foreign lines verbatim
    73	    }
    74	    const stripped = stripTranscript(parsed);
    75	    const next = JSON.stringify(stripped);
    76	    if (next !== JSON.stringify(parsed)) {
    77	      changed = true;
    78	      return next;
    79	    }
    80	    return line;
    81	  });
    82	  if (changed) atomicWriteText(io.fs, path, lines.join('\n'));
    83	}

    85	/**
    86	 * `baton purge-transcript` — scrub the opt-in transcript field from EVERY
    87	 * retained copy under .handoff/ (active snapshot, .bak, journal, history
    88	 * freezes + rotated journals, diagnostics log). Marker-guarded so an
    89	 * interrupted purge resumes until the whole tree is clean; runs under the repo
    90	 * lock so a live foreign session blocks it entirely.
    91	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    92	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    93	 */
    94	export async function cmdPurgeTranscript(args, io) {
    95	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, {});
    96	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'purge-transcript', parsed.error);
    97	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    98	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    99	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
   100	  const markerPath = `${p.dir}/purge.marker.json`;
   101	
   102	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(p.dir)) {
   103	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { purged: 0, note: 'no .handoff directory — nothing to purge' } });
   104	    else io.stdout.write('purge-transcript: no .handoff directory — nothing to purge\n');
   105	    return 0;
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  // Jail check BEFORE the lock: acquiring the lock mkdirs inside .handoff, so
   109	  // a symlinked tree must be refused before any write lands through the link.
   110	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
   111	  if (!safe.ok) {
   112	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'unsafe-tree', msg: safe.problem } });
   113	    else io.stderr.write(`baton purge-transcript: ${safe.problem}\n`);
   114	    return 1;
   115	  }
   116	
   117	  // Auto-resume (gate-2 minor 16): a leftover marker means an earlier purge
   118	  // was interrupted mid-scrub — this run finishes the job.
   119	  if (io.fs.existsSync(markerPath)) {
   120	    io.stderr.write('baton purge-transcript: resuming an interrupted purge (marker found) — re-scrubbing the whole tree\n');
   121	  }
   122	
   123	  try {
   124	    withLock(root, io, () => {
   125	      atomicWriteJson(io.fs, markerPath, { startedAt: io.now() });
   126	      for (const file of walk(io, p.dir)) {
   127	        if (file === markerPath) continue;
   128	        if (/\.(ndjson|jsonl)$/.test(file)) scrubLinesFile(io, file);
   129	        else if (/\.(json|bak)$/.test(file)) scrubJsonFile(io, file);
   130	      }
   131	      io.fs.unlinkSync(markerPath);
   132	    });
   133	  } catch (err) {
   134	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err);
   135	    const code = err instanceof LockHeldError ? 'lock-held' : 'purge-failed';
   136	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code, msg } });
   137	    else io.stderr.write(`baton purge-transcript: ${msg}\n`);
   138	    return 1;
   139	  }
   140	
   141	  if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { note: 'transcript fields removed from every retained copy under .handoff/' } });
   142	  else io.stdout.write('purge-transcript: transcript fields removed from every retained copy under .handoff/\n');
   143	  return 0;
   144	}

    46	/** Parse `git worktree list --porcelain` into [{path, branch}]. @param {string} out */
    47	function parseWorktreeList(out) {
    48	  /** @type {Array<{path: string, branch: string | null}>} */
    49	  const entries = [];
    50	  for (const block of String(out).split(/\n\n+/)) {
    51	    const path = block.match(/^worktree (.+)$/m)?.[1];
    52	    if (!path) continue;
    53	    const branch = block.match(/^branch refs\/heads\/(.+)$/m)?.[1] ?? null;
    54	    entries.push({ path, branch });
    55	  }
    56	  return entries;
    57	}

    59	/**
    60	 * Ensure both seat worktrees exist on their namespaced branches and that
    61	 * `.worktrees/` is gitignored. Idempotent: an existing seat is left alone.
    62	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io

    64	 */
    65	export async function setupWorktrees(root, io) {
    66	  const p = worktreePaths(root);
    67	
    68	  const gitignorePath = `${root}/.gitignore`;
    69	  const existing = io.fs.existsSync(gitignorePath) ? io.fs.readFileSync(gitignorePath, 'utf8') : '';
    70	  const ensured = ensureIgnoreLine(existing, '.worktrees/');
    71	  if (ensured.changed) io.fs.writeFileSync(gitignorePath, ensured.text);
    72

    90	/**
    91	 * Preflight before a child runs in a seat: the worktree is listed, its index
    92	 * is clean, and HEAD sits on the expected branch. Refusals name the failed
    93	 * check and never issue destructive git.
    94	 * @param {string} root @param {{seat: string, branch: string}} target @param {any} io
    95	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true} | {ok: false, check: string, refusal: string}>}
    96	 */
    97	export async function preflightWorktree(root, target, io) {
    98	  const path = worktreePaths(root).seats[target.seat];
    99	  const listed = parseWorktreeList((await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).stdout);
   100	  if (!listed.some((e) => e.path === path)) {
   101	    return { ok: false, check: 'missing-worktree', refusal: `worktree ${path} is not listed by git — run setup or self-heal first` };
   102	  }
   103	  const status = (await git(io, path, ['status', '--porcelain'])).stdout.trim();
   104	  if (status.length > 0) {
   105	    return { ok: false, check: 'dirty-index', refusal: `worktree ${path} has a dirty index/working tree — a clean seat is required before a child runs` };
   106	  }
   107	  const head = (await git(io, path, ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'])).stdout.trim();
   108	  if (head !== target.branch) {
   109	    return { ok: false, check: 'wrong-branch', refusal: `worktree ${path} HEAD is on '${head}', expected branch '${target.branch}'` };
   110	  }
   111	  return { ok: true };
   112	}
   113	
   114	/**
   115	 * Postflight after a child: HEAD still on the expected branch (checked in the
   116	 * seat cwd) and main unmoved from the pre-child capture.
   117	 * @param {string} root @param {{seat: string, branch: string, mainSha: string}} target @param {any} io
   118	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true} | {ok: false, check: string, refusal: string}>}
   119	 */
   120	export async function postflightWorktree(root, target, io) {
   121	  const path = worktreePaths(root).seats[target.seat];
   122	  const head = (await git(io, path, ['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD'])).stdout.trim();
   123	  if (head !== target.branch) {
   124	    return { ok: false, check: 'head-drift', refusal: `the child left HEAD on '${head}' instead of the expected branch '${target.branch}'` };
   125	  }
   126	  const main = (await git(io, root, ['rev-parse', 'main'])).stdout.trim();
   127	  if (main !== target.mainSha) {
   128	    return { ok: false, check: 'main-moved', refusal: `main moved under the child (was ${target.mainSha}, now ${main}) — only the merger writes main` };
   129	  }
   130	  return { ok: true };
   131	}

   133	/**
   134	 * Full-range attribution scan over main..branch — the merge gate. Every
   135	 * commit must be authored AND committed by the sole author, with no forbidden
   136	 * AI-attribution trailer in the body. The range is never windowed.
   137	 * @param {string} root @param {string} branch @param {any} io
   138	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true} | {ok: false, offending: string, reason: string}>}
   139	 */
   140	export async function attributionScan(root, branch, io) {
   141	  const out = (await git(io, root, ['log', `main..${branch}`, `--format=${LOG_FORMAT}`])).stdout;
   142	  for (const record of String(out).split('\x1e')) {
   143	    if (record.trim().length === 0) continue;
   144	    const [sha, an, ae, cn, ce, body = ''] = record.replace(/^\n/, '').split('\x00');
   145	    if (an !== SOLE_AUTHOR.name || ae !== SOLE_AUTHOR.email) {
   146	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} has a foreign author identity (${an} <${ae}>) — sole-author is required` };
   147	    }
   148	    if (cn !== SOLE_AUTHOR.name || ce !== SOLE_AUTHOR.email) {
   149	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} has a foreign committer identity (${cn} <${ce}>) — sole-author is required` };
   150	    }
   151	    if (TRAILER_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(body))) {
   152	      return { ok: false, offending: sha, reason: `commit ${sha} carries a forbidden AI-attribution trailer (co-authored/generated-with/emoji) in its message` };
   153	    }
   154	  }
   155	  return { ok: true };
   156	}

   158	const mergeLockPath = (/** @type {string} */ root) => `${root}/.handoff/loop/merge.lock`;
   159	
   160	/**
   161	 * Merge an approved subtask branch into main — one guarded transaction:
   162	 * acquire the merge lock (a held lock refuses), gate on the attribution scan,
   163	 * merge at the repo root, abort-and-park on conflict, then ff-only sync both
   164	 * seats. The lock is released on EVERY exit path after acquisition.
   165	 * @param {string} root @param {{branch: string}} input @param {any} io
   166	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: true, branch: string} | {ok: false, reason: string}>}
   167	 */
   168	export async function mergeSubtask(root, input, io) {
   169	  const lock = mergeLockPath(root);
   170	  if (io.fs.existsSync(lock)) {
   171	    return { ok: false, reason: `the merge lock at ${lock} is held by another merger — refusing a concurrent merge` };
   172	  }
   173	  ensureDir(io.fs, `${root}/.handoff/loop`);
   174	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, lock, { host: io.host, pid: io.pid, at: io.now() });
   175	  try {
   176	    const scan = await attributionScan(root, input.branch, io);
   177	    if (scan.ok !== true) return { ok: false, reason: scan.reason };
   178	
   179	    try {
   180	      await git(io, root, ['merge', input.branch]);
   181	    } catch (err) {
   182	      // Conflict (or any merge failure): abort, never auto-resolve — park.
   183	      try {
   184	        await git(io, root, ['merge', '--abort']);
   185	      } catch {
   186	        // Nothing to abort — the failure predates a merge state.
   187	      }
   188	      const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.stdout || /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message || String(err);
   189	      return { ok: false, reason: `merge conflict — aborted and parked for the operator: ${String(msg).split('\n')[0]}` };
   190	    }
   191	
   192	    const seats = worktreePaths(root).seats;
   193	    for (const seat of SEATS) {
   194	      try {
   195	        await git(io, seats[seat], ['merge', '--ff-only', 'main']);
   196	      } catch (err) {
   197	        const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.stderr || /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message || String(err);
   198	        return { ok: false, reason: `worktree wt-${seat} could not fast-forward to main — corruption signal, parked: ${String(msg).split('\n')[0]}` };
   199	      }
   200	    }
   201	    return { ok: true, branch: input.branch };
   202	  } finally {
   203	    try {
   204	      if (io.fs.existsSync(lock)) io.fs.unlinkSync(lock);
   205	    } catch {
   206	      // Best effort — a leaked lock is visible and operator-recoverable.
   207	    }
   208	  }
   209	}

   211	/**
   212	 * Self-heal a raw-deleted seat: git still lists it but the directory is gone
   213	 * — prune the stale metadata and re-add on the same branch.
   214	 * @param {string} root @param {{seat: string, branch: string}} target @param {any} io
   215	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: boolean, healed: boolean}>}
   216	 */
   217	export async function selfHealWorktree(root, target, io) {
   218	  const path = worktreePaths(root).seats[target.seat];
   219	  const listed = parseWorktreeList((await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).stdout);
   220	  const stale = listed.some((e) => e.path === path) && !io.fs.existsSync(path);
   221	  if (!stale) return { ok: true, healed: false };

   227	/**
   228	 * Tear down BOTH seats: remove the worktrees and delete their namespaced
   229	 * branches. Anything outside .worktrees/wt-* or baton/wt-* is never touched,
   230	 * so a teardown leaves the repo a plain git repo (acceptance constraint 5).
   231	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io
   232	 * @returns {Promise<{ok: boolean, removed: string[]}>}
   233	 */
   234	export async function teardownWorktrees(root, io) {
   235	  const p = worktreePaths(root);
   236	  const listed = parseWorktreeList((await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).stdout);
   237	  /** @type {string[]} */
   238	  const removed = [];
   239	  for (const seat of SEATS) {
   240	    const entry = listed.find((e) => e.path === p.seats[seat]);
   241	    if (!entry) continue;
   242	    await git(io, root, ['worktree', 'remove', '--force', p.seats[seat]]);
   243	    // Delete the seat's CURRENT branch and its setup base branch — a seat
   244	    // that moved on to subtask branches orphans its base otherwise
   245	    // (acceptance constraint 5: teardown leaves a plain git repo). Only
   246	    // namespaced branches are ever deleted.
   247	    /** @type {Set<string>} */
   248	    const toDelete = new Set();
   249	    if (entry.branch && WORKTREE_BRANCH_RE.test(entry.branch)) toDelete.add(entry.branch);
   250	    toDelete.add(seatBranch(seat));
   251	    for (const branch of toDelete) {
   252	      if (!WORKTREE_BRANCH_RE.test(branch)) continue;
   253	      try {
   254	        await git(io, root, ['branch', '-D', branch]);
   255	      } catch {
   256	        // Already gone (current === base, or deleted earlier) — fine.
   257	      }
   258	    }
   259	    removed.push(seat);
   260	  }
   261	  return { ok: true, removed };
   262	}

   264	/**

   270	export async function deleteBranch(root, branch, io) {

   273	  }

   275	  return { ok: true };

   117	/** Recursively collect every file's content under a memfs directory. */
   118	function allFiles(io, dir) {
   119	  /** @type {{path: string, content: string}[]} */
   120	  const out = [];
   121	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(dir)) return out;
   122	  for (const name of io.fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
   123	    const p = `${dir}/${name}`;
   124	    if (io.fs.statSync(p).isDirectory()) out.push(...allFiles(io, p));
   125	    else out.push({ path: p, content: io.fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8') });
   126	  }
   127	  return out;
   128	}

    58	/**
    59	 * A recording fake git. `responses` maps an args-substring (longest match wins)
    60	 * to a canned result; { reject:true } models a nonzero git exit. An UNSTUBBED
    61	 * git invocation REJECTS (ENOSTUB) — a test must declare its command surface.
    62	 */
    63	function fakeGit(responses = {}, lockProbe = null) {
    64	  const keys = Object.keys(responses).sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);
    65	  const calls = /** @type {any[]} */ ([]);
    66	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = [], /** @type {any} */ opts = {}) => {
    67	    const argstr = args.join(' ');
    68	    // Record whether the merge lock is present AT CALL TIME (finding 2): proves
    69	    // mutating git ran under the acquired lock.
    70	    calls.push({ cmd, args, argstr, cwd: opts?.cwd, lockPresent: typeof lockProbe === 'function' ? lockProbe() : undefined });
    71	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
    72	    const k = keys.find((key) => argstr.includes(key));
    73	    if (k === undefined) return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(`unstubbed git: ${argstr}`), { code: 'ENOSTUB' }));
    74	    const r = responses[k];
    75	    if (r?.reject) return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error(r.stderr || 'git failed'), { code: r.code ?? 1, stdout: r.stdout ?? '', stderr: r.stderr ?? '' }));
    76	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: r?.stdout ?? '', stderr: r?.stderr ?? '' });
    77	  };
    78	  fn.calls = calls;
    79	  fn.git = () => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git');
    80	  fn.issued = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re) => calls.some((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr));
    81	  fn.withCwd = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re, /** @type {string} */ cwd) => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr) && c.cwd === cwd);
    82	  fn.matching = (/** @type {RegExp} */ re) => calls.filter((c) => c.cmd === 'git' && re.test(c.argstr));
    83	  return fn;
    84	}

     6	/**
     7	 * `baton remap` — resolve the committed role matrix for a destination platform.
     8	 * Read-only: prints assignments, never mutates the bundle (receive owns that).
     9	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    10	 * @returns {number}
    11	 */
    12	export function cmdRemap(args, io) {
    13	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { to: 'string', avoid: 'string', 'native-only': 'boolean' });
    14	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'remap', parsed.error);
    15	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    16	  const to = typeof flags.to === 'string' ? flags.to : null;
    17	  if (!to) return usageError(io, flags, 'remap', '--to <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required');
    18	  const pErr = platformError(to);
    19	  if (pErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'remap', pErr);
    20	
    21	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    22	  const { config, errors } = loadConfig(root, io);
    23	  if (!config) {
    24	    const msg = errors.map((e) => (e.path ? `${e.path}: ${e.msg}` : e.msg)).join('; ');
    25	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'bad-config', msg } });
    26	    else io.stderr.write(`baton remap: ${msg}\n`);
    27	    return 1;
    28	  }
    29	
    30	  const avoid = typeof flags.avoid === 'string' ? flags.avoid.split(',') : [];
    31	  const { assignments, notes } = resolveRoles({
    32	    config,
    33	    to,
    34	    avoid,
    35	    nativeOnly: flags['native-only'] === true,
    36	    // The fresh doctor probe cache feeds eligibility (gate-2 major 13):
    37	    // rate-limited platforms are skipped like avoid[] entries; a stale or
    38	    // absent cache resolves offline with degraded flags.
    39	    probes: readProbeCache(root, io),
    40	  });
    41	
    42	  if (flags.json) {
    43	    emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { assignments, notes } });
    44	  } else {
    45	    for (const [role, a] of Object.entries(assignments)) {
    46	      io.stdout.write(`${role}: ${a.platform ?? '—'}/${a.model ?? '—'}${a.effort ? `@${a.effort}` : ''} (${a.mode})\n`);
    47	    }
    48	  }
    49	  return 0;

    19	 * low-confidence heuristic (e.g. Cursor's "quota exceeded") must not silently
    20	 * drive an avoid[] decision — the caller warns and defers to explicit intake.
    21	 * @param {string} reason @param {string} originPlatform @param {any} io
    22	 * @returns {{class: string | null, confidence: string | null}}
    23	 */
    24	function classifyReason(reason, originPlatform, io) {
    25	  try {
    26	    const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    27	    const verdict = classify({ text: reason, exitCode: 0, platform: originPlatform, table, structured: null });
    28	    return verdict.class === 'ok' ? { class: null, confidence: null } : { class: verdict.class, confidence: verdict.confidence };
    29	  } catch {
    30	    return { class: null, confidence: null };
    31	  }
    32	}
    33	
    34	/**
    35	 * Effective intake: the sealed bundle already records who handed off and why,
    36	 * so the 'unknown'/'unspecified' CLI sentinels default from it (audit finding:
    37	 * the documented resume command rendered "Handed off from unknown" straight
    38	 * after sealing a real origin/reason). Explicit intake always wins. Pure and
    39	 * bundle-deterministic, so prepare and commit derive identical tokens.
    40	 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @returns {ReceiveOpts}
    41	 */
    42	function effectiveIntake(bundle, opts) {
    43	  const originSentinel = opts.origin === 'unknown' || opts.origin === undefined;
    44	  const reasonSentinel = opts.reason === 'unspecified' || opts.reason === undefined;
    45	  const sealedOrigin = typeof bundle?.origin?.platform === 'string' && bundle.origin.platform !== 'unknown' ? bundle.origin.platform : null;
    46	  const sealedReason = typeof bundle?.handoff?.reason === 'string' && bundle.handoff.reason.length > 0 ? bundle.handoff.reason : null;
    47	  return {
    48	    ...opts,
    49	    origin: originSentinel && sealedOrigin ? sealedOrigin : opts.origin,
    50	    reason: reasonSentinel && sealedReason ? sealedReason : opts.reason,
    51	  };
    52	}
    53	
    54	// The bound token inputs, in the fixed order the structured token serializes
    55	// them. The human names power drift diagnosis: a stale-token rejection names
    56	// exactly which input(s) moved instead of listing six guesses.
    57	const TOKEN_FIELDS = /** @type {const} */ ([
    58	  ['generation', 'bundle generation'],
    59	  ['journalSeq', 'journal seq'],
    60	  ['handoffStatus', 'handoff status'],
    61	  ['receives', 'receive count'],
    62	  ['origin', 'intake origin'],
    63	  ['reason', 'intake reason'],
    64	  ['reasonClass', 'intake reason-class'],
    65	  ['configDigest', 'config'],
    66	  ['gitDigest', 'git state'],
    67	  ['probesDigest', 'probe cache'],
    68	  ['platform', 'target platform'],
    69	  ['sessionHint', 'target session'],
    70	]);
    71	const TOKEN_PREFIX = 'rcpt1';
    72	
    73	/**
    74	 * The revision fingerprint the receipt token derives from. Every field is a
    75	 * bound input: any drift between prepare and commit re-derives a different
    76	 * token, so a stale receipt can never commit (plan §Concurrency).
    77	 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
    78	 * @returns {Record<string, any>}
    79	 */
    80	function tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io) {
    81	  let configDigest = 'absent';
    82	  try {
    83	    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
    84	  } catch {
    85	    // no config — 'absent' is itself a bound value
    86	  }
    87	  return {
    88	    generation: bundle.generation,
    89	    journalSeq: bundle.journalSeq,
    90	    // The seal state is a bound input too (gate-2 fix): a competing receiver
    91	    // that lands between this token's derivation and its commit changes
    92	    // status/receive_log, so the loser's token cannot re-derive.
    93	    handoffStatus: bundle.handoff?.status ?? null,
    94	    receives: Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) ? bundle.handoff.receive_log.length : 0,
    95	    origin: opts.origin,
    96	    reason: opts.reason,
    97	    // Explicit --reason-class is a bound intake input (gate-2 iter-2 M4): it
    98	    // changes the avoid[] decision, so a change between prepare and commit is
    99	    // drift that must re-prepare.
   100	    reasonClass: opts.reasonClass ?? null,
   101	    configDigest,
   102	    gitDigest: dedupeKey(opts.gitSnapshot ?? null),
   103	    probesDigest: dedupeKey(opts.probes ?? null),
   104	    platform: opts.platform,
   105	    sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
   106	  };
   107	}
   108	
   109	/**
   110	 * Structured receipt token: a fixed-order join of per-input digests. Equality
   111	 * still gates commit exactly as the old opaque hash did; the structure only
   112	 * buys DIAGNOSIS — a mismatch can name the drifted input(s).
   113	 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   114	 */
   115	function deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io) {
   116	  const inputs = tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io);
   117	  return `${TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + TOKEN_FIELDS.map(([key]) => dedupeKey(inputs[key] ?? null).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
   118	}
   119	
   120	/**
   121	 * Name the inputs whose digests differ between two structured tokens.
   122	 * @param {string} presented @param {string} expected @returns {string[]}
   123	 */
   124	function driftedInputs(presented, expected) {
   125	  const a = presented.split('.');
   126	  const b = expected.split('.');
   127	  if (a[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || b[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || a.length !== b.length) return [];
   128	  return TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((_, i) => a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]).map(([, name]) => name);
   129	}
   130	
   131	/**
   132	 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   133	 * @returns {string[]} staleness/degradation warnings
   134	 */
   135	function stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io) {
   136	  /** @type {string[]} */
   137	  const warnings = [];
   138	  if (bundle.handoff.status === 'open') {
   139	    warnings.push('source bundle is unsealed (open) — the handoff was never finalized; treating this as a degraded (limit-death) receive');
   140	  }
   141	  const ref = bundle.handoff.finalizedAt ?? bundle.updatedAt;
   142	  const ageMs = Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(ref);
   143	  if (Number.isFinite(ageMs) && ageMs > STALE_AFTER_MS) {
   144	    warnings.push(`bundle finalized ${Math.round(ageMs / 3_600_000)}h ago (staleness threshold 12h) — re-verify before continuing`);
   145	  }
   146	  const g = opts.gitSnapshot;
   147	  if (g && bundle.git) {
   148	    if (bundle.git.headSha !== g.headSha) {
   149	      warnings.push(`HEAD moved since capture: bundle recorded ${bundle.git.headSha}, working tree now ${g.headSha}`);
   150	    }
   151	    if (bundle.git.dirty !== g.dirty) {
   152	      warnings.push(`dirty-state mismatch: bundle captured dirty=${bundle.git.dirty}, working tree now dirty=${g.dirty}`);
   153	    }
   154	  }
   155	  return warnings;
   156	}
   157	
   158	/**
   159	 * Phase 1 of the receive transaction: validate, resolve roles, render the
   160	 * resume prompt, and return a one-time receipt token. Mutates NOTHING — the
   161	 * token is self-contained (a fingerprint hash), never a persisted record.
   162	 * @param {string} root @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   163	 * @returns {{token: string, prompt: string, assignments: Record<string, any>, warnings: string[]}}
   164	 */
   165	export function prepare(root, opts, io) {
   166	  const { bundle, warnings: loadWarnings } = loadBundle(root, io);
   167	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive`);
   168	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   169	
   170	  const warnings = [...loadWarnings, ...stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io)];
   171	
   172	  const { config, errors } = loadConfig(root, io);
   173	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
   174	  let assignments = {};
   175	  if (config) {
   176	    // The dead origin comes from the BUNDLE first (its sealed reasonClass and
   177	    // recorded origin platform); typed intake only fills the gaps — a user
   178	    // should not need to retype the verbatim limit string to keep roles off
   179	    // the platform that died (gate-2 reviewer-b finding 4). Confidence gates
   180	    // auto-avoidance (gate-2 iter-2 M4): an explicit --reason-class or a sealed
   181	    // reasonClass is trusted; a live text classification only auto-avoids at
   182	    // medium+ confidence, else it warns and defers to explicit intake.
   183	    let reasonClass;
   184	    let confidence;
   185	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
   186	      reasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
   187	      confidence = 'high'; // explicit user intake
   188	    } else if (typeof bundle.handoff?.reasonClass === 'string') {
   189	      reasonClass = bundle.handoff.reasonClass;
   190	      confidence = 'high'; // trusted seal
   191	    } else {
   192	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
   193	      reasonClass = v.class;
   194	      confidence = v.confidence;
   195	    }
   196	    const deadOrigin =
   197	      typeof bundle.origin?.platform === 'string' && bundle.origin.platform !== 'unknown' ? bundle.origin.platform : opts.origin;
   198	    /** @type {string[]} */
   199	    let avoid = [];
   200	    if (reasonClass === 'usage-limit') {
   201	      if (confidence === 'low') {
   202	        warnings.push(
   203	          `the switch reason matched a usage-limit heuristic only at LOW confidence — not auto-avoiding ${deadOrigin}; pass --reason-class usage-limit to confirm the failover away from it`,
   204	        );
   205	      } else {
   206	        avoid = [deadOrigin];
   207	      }
   208	    }
   209	    assignments = resolveRoles({ config, to: opts.platform, avoid, nativeOnly: false, probes: opts.probes ?? null }).assignments;
   210	  } else {
   211	    warnings.push(`role matrix unavailable (${errors.map((e) => e.msg).join('; ')}) — no role table in this prompt`);
   212	  }
   213	
   214	  const prompt = renderResumePrompt({ bundle, assignments, warnings, origin: opts.origin, reason: opts.reason });
   215	  return { token: deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io), prompt, assignments, warnings };
   216	}
   217	
   218	/**
   219	 * Phase 2: one atomic transition. Re-derives every bound input from current
   220	 * disk state + opts and rejects ANY drift (throws, zero mutation). On match:
   221	 * writes the received seal, archives it via a 'receive' rotation, then opens a
   222	 * fresh writable generation owned by the receiving platform/session.
   223	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   224	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   225	 */
   226	export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
   227	  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
   228	  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
   229	  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
   230	  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
   231	}
   232	
   233	/**
   234	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
   235	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   236	 */
   237	function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
   238	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
   239	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
   240	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   241	
   242	  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
   243	  if (expected !== token) {
   244	    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
   245	    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
   246	    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
   247	    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
   248	    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.
   249	    const receipt = dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16);
   250	    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);
   251	    if (landed) {
   252	      return { adopted: false, alreadyCommitted: true, generation: bundle.generation, archivedTo: null };
   253	    }
   254	    const drifted = driftedInputs(token, expected);
   255	    const detail = drifted.length > 0 ? `drifted input(s): ${drifted.join(', ')}` : 'a bound input drifted since prepare';
   256	    throw new Error(
   257	      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
   258	    );
   259	  }
   260	
   261	  const degraded = bundle.handoff.status !== 'sealed';
   262	  const receiveEntry = {
   263	    origin: opts.origin,
   264	    reason: opts.reason,
   265	    at: io.now(),
   266	    // The receipt digest keys the idempotent-retry detection above.
   267	    receipt: dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16),
   268	    ...(degraded ? { degradedSeal: true } : {}),
   269	  };
   270	
   271	  // The degraded seal must NOT persist a LOW-confidence classification (iter-3
   272	  // F10): a sealed reasonClass is trusted as high-confidence by the next
   273	  // prepare, so laundering a low-confidence heuristic here would silently
   274	  // auto-avoid the origin one hop later. Explicit intake is high-confidence and
   275	  // seals; a live classification seals ONLY at medium+ confidence, else null
   276	  // (the next receive re-classifies the reason text at its true confidence).
   277	  let sealedReasonClass = null;
   278	  if (degraded) {
   279	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
   280	      sealedReasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
   281	    } else {
   282	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
   283	      sealedReasonClass = v.confidence === 'low' ? null : v.class;
   284	    }
   285	  }
   286	
   287	  const receivedSeal = {
   288	    ...bundle,
   289	    updatedAt: io.now(),
   290	    handoff: {
   291	      ...bundle.handoff,
   292	      status: 'received',
   293	      ...(degraded
   294	        ? {
   295	            reason: opts.reason,
   296	            reasonClass: sealedReasonClass,
   297	            finalizedAt: io.now(),
   298	          }
   299	        : {}),
   300	      receive_log: [...bundle.handoff.receive_log, receiveEntry],
   301	    },
   302	  };
   303	
   304	  // Freeze order: the received seal is written first so the 'receive' rotation
   305	  // archives exactly that state (never the pre-commit bundle). All three
   306	  // mutations run under the SAME lock acquisition, fence-checked per write.
   307	  writeSnapshotIn(root, receivedSeal, io, fence);
   308	  const archivedTo = rotateJournalIn(root, 'receive', io, fence);
   309	
   310	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   311	  const next = {
   312	    ...receivedSeal,
   313	    generation: bundle.generation + 1,
   314	    origin: {
   315	      platform: opts.platform,
   316	      model: config?.defaults?.[opts.platform] ?? 'unknown',
   317	      sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
   318	      unstable: opts.sessionUnstable === true,
   319	    },
   320	    // The fresh writable generation has NO switch reason yet (iter-4 I3): the
   321	    // sealed reason/reasonClass/finalizedAt/toPlatformHint describe the PRIOR
   322	    // handoff, not this one. Carrying them forward made the next prepare trust a
   323	    // stale class as a high-confidence seal (silently auto-avoiding the healthy
   324	    // adopted origin) and poisoned both the 12 h staleness reference and the
   325	    // sessionStart limit-hit signal. Keep only receive_log (the audit chain).
   326	    handoff: { ...receivedSeal.handoff, status: 'open', reason: null, reasonClass: null, finalizedAt: null, toPlatformHint: null },
   327	  };
   328	  writeSnapshotIn(root, next, io, fence);
   329	
   330	  return { adopted: true, generation: next.generation, archivedTo };
   331	}

Surfaces: (1) **repo `.codex/hooks.json`** (written by `init --codex`, merged never clobbered): `Stop` → mechanical checkpoint, `PreCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint, `SessionStart` → pending-handoff notice via injected context. No StopFailure equivalent exists on Codex, so a limit death is bounded by the last Stop checkpoint (one turn worst case). (2) `.agents/skills/baton-handoff/SKILL.md` per the Agent Skills standard — carries the receive/handoff protocol, invoked as `$baton-handoff` or by description match. (3) Repo `AGENTS.md` Handoff Protocol section as the always-on instruction layer (narrative checkpoints after subtasks / before risky ops / at wind-down). (4) `~/.codex/prompts/*.md` demoted to **legacy fallback only** (deprecated upstream), written only with `--with-legacy-prompts`. The notify shim is **cut** — hooks make it obsolete; `~/.codex/config.toml` is never touched. **Trust gate** (verified, Gate-1 iteration 2): Codex requires per-definition review of non-managed command hooks — trust is recorded against the hook's hash, and new/changed hooks are skipped until re-trusted via `/hooks`. Setup and doctor therefore report four distinct states per hook — installed / enabled / **trusted** / observed-executing (canary event) — and the fidelity claim is gated on the canary, with setup guiding the user through `/hooks` when review is pending. Hook definitions include `commandWindows` overrides. Fidelity statement ships verbatim in README + doctor: mechanical staleness ≤ 1 turn via Stop hook **once trusted**; narrative staleness bounded by protocol compliance; git state always re-derived at receive. Requires codex-cli >= 0.144 (doctor enforces; older versions fall back to protocol-only Tier C with an explicit warning).

Usage-limit → the ordered transaction on the REAL command machinery: loop position checkpointed into the bundle under the supervisor session BEFORE the seal; finalize with reasonClass usage-limit (degraded-open path also pinned); receive prepare+commit back-to-back with identical flags/session; zero .handoff/loop writes across the transaction (fs spy); injected window drift → one automatic re-prepare retry; second consecutive stale → park; relaunch assignment avoids the dead origin platform; total exhaustion → park with the classifier's resumeAt hint; deterministic from injected io. Non-limit exit → retry once then park (attempt-driven), no bundle transitions. Usage-limit → the ordered transaction on the REAL command machinery: loop position checkpointed into the bundle under the supervisor session BEFORE the seal; finalize with reasonClass usage-limit (degraded-open path also pinned); receive prepare+commit back-to-back with identical flags/session; zero .handoff/loop writes across the transaction (fs spy); injected window drift → one automatic re-prepare retry; second consecutive stale → park; relaunch assignment avoids the dead origin platform; total exhaustion → park with the classifier's resumeAt hint; deterministic from injected io. reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3521:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:4558:docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

Non-limit exit → retry once then park (attempt-driven), no bundle transitions. Model-unavailable at spawn → dead {platform, model} added to avoidEntries, re-resolve to the SAME platform's next entry, relaunch, no seal/receive. Usage-limit → the ordered transaction on the REAL command machinery: loop position checkpointed into the bundle under the supervisor session BEFORE the seal; finalize with reasonClass usage-limit (degraded-open path also pinned); receive prepare+commit back-to-back with identical flags/session; zero .handoff/loop writes across the transaction (fs spy); injected window drift → one automatic re-prepare retry; second consecutive stale → park; relaunch assignment avoids the dead origin platform; total exhaustion → park with the classifier's resumeAt hint; deterministic from injected io. The test-author flags one design seam for your judgment: `hooks.beforeCommit()` — a test-only injection point used to mutate git state inside the prepare→commit window; production passes nothing.

reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3730:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6324:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:320:    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3731:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6325:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:348:    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3774:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6693:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-state/test-verifier/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:2542:     4	  "description": "Usage-limit failover for AI coding sessions across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor: checkpoint, hand off, resume with remapped model roles.",
reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3775:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6696:reviews/2026-07-12-gate-2-final/reviewer-a/iteration-05/raw-output.txt:182:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3795:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6838:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:9467:  1677	   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-19-gate-2-milestone-b/reviewer-a/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:3877:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7378:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1420:   299	     9	Research confirmed the white space: Databricks' Omnigent (June 2026) is the closest analog but replaces native configs with its own YAML and ships **no usage-limit failover**; nothing else does harness-level failover either (closest is model-level switching).
